A highlight for me was the dish of asparagus, morel mushrooms, and wild garlic sauce—rich and earthy. The scampi was full of umami, with the seafood flavor deeply infused into the sauce. This was followed by grilled turbot accompanied by carrot, lovage, and a beautifully crafted sauce that tied everything together.

For the main course, I opted for the spaghetti with guanciale, cured egg, and truffle—perfectly executed and deeply satisfying. My client chose the homemade tagliatelle topped with Giant Carabineros, which looked excellent, though the $88 supplement felt a bit excessive.

Another standout dish I tried was the grilled Irish duck, paired with eggplant, tomato, burrata, and basil. The combination balanced the richness of the meat perfectly. The duck was tender with crispy skin and matched beautifully with its accompanying sauce. For beef lovers, the A5 Wagyu was also available as an alternative.

Dessert offered a wide selection, from artisanal ice creams to handcrafted chocolates. We paired the meal with an American Oregon Chardonnay, which was thoroughly enjoyable.

TL;DR: A high-end steakhouse masquerading as a BBQ joint.

I visited Burnt Ends during a business trip to Singapore, expecting the "Australian-style BBQ" promised by their description. As an amateur pitmaster, the name alone had me hooked; burnt ends are the holy grail of brisket. I was ready for an interesting Aussie spin (perhaps kangaroo or crocodile?) and maybe a Southeast Asian fusion take.

The restaurant smells amazing, but the disappointment started the moment I opened the menu. Despite the name, there are no actual burnt ends. No ribs, no pulled pork, no brisket. It’s like going to "Wagyu Palace" only to find they only serve fried chicken sandwiches. Beyond the wine list, the "Australian" influence was nowhere to be found.

If you ignore the BBQ branding, what you’re left with is a high-end steakhouse operating in "try-hard" mode. The appetizers and vegetable sides are creative and clearly designed to court food critics. The appetizers were expertly crafted, and the steak cooked to perfection, but the entire evening was seasoned with the bitter taste of false expectations.

The service was inconsistent. While attentive at first, the staff vanished for a full 30 minutes between the appetizers and the mains. For a premium establishment, that’s an excessive gap.

Then, there are the bathrooms. To get there, you navigate a long, dark hallway only to find stalls that look like they belong in a dive bar. They were dirty, and my colleagues reported a total lack of hand towels and toilet paper. It’s a jarring contrast to the fine dining price tag.

Verdict: 2/5 Stars
-1 Star: Misleading branding (Not a BBQ restaurant).
-1 Star: Inconsistent service and odd pacing.
-1 Star: Poorly maintained, "dive bar" quality facilities.

Long story short, Burnt Ends has some decent culinary standards, but very low service and hospitality standards. Just like you, I’ve travelled all over the world, and Burnt Ends is simply not worth it.

At the end of the meal, it became clear the steak had been discarded due to a miscommunication. Staff were apologetic and offered complimentary tea while preparing a new portion, but the replacement was only ~150g compared to the 500–600g that was left behind.

It was disheartening to see such a premium cut of wagyu go to waste, especially when I had clearly communicated the request twice. I was left wondering why the assumption was made that we would want to discard such a substantial portion of food.

That said, the atmosphere, food quality, and the genuine friendliness of the staff made the evening memorable. It was just a bittersweet ending to what otherwise would have been a seamless dining experience.
We have enjoyed fine dining around the world_ BB far exceeds all. Immaculate service. Very attentive to detail. Food presentation beyond words. Taste delicate.

We literal got kicked out from our table because the manager/(or owner) said someone is waiting for a table. This manager was not seen the whole time until when she appeared to kick us out, she was a skinny female in her 40s. Our dinner took 2 hours for the ahmakase and there were other tables that were seated longer than ours. This happened around 9:00 PM and restaurant closes at 10 PM. I later confirmed that there is no time limit for our table with one of the servers. There is no way they could earn a Michelin star with this kind of unacceptable rude practice. And on our way out I heard a couple was complaining about being rushed out too. So, it is obvious that this place is maximizing profit at the expense of their customers; and they have a Michelin 1 star?? We are a group of middle age professionals and business owners that are polite, soft-spoken and well-traveled. I even pointed out an error of our bill that they forgot to include the bottle of wine we ordered, and few minutes later they just kicked us out while we were trying to finish our tea. My wife was laughing at me with what I got for being a nice guy.

The food was not a much better experience. I have lived in Thailand for 20 years and there were couple Thai friends eating with us at this dinner. We all agreed that the main courses resemble Thai food too much and in a bad way, and they were below average in overall quality. All the main courses were almost cold and this is not acceptable. So, you should believe the other 1 and 2 star reviews saying that this is a tourist trap and locals would avoid it.

Added on 10/March/2026:

Someone from the restaurant's corporate headquarters sent a email essentially saying they are sorry for how I felt but they had done nothing wrong. They even attached a fine print of a legal notice of a 1.5 hour time limit on the table that nobody seemed to have mentioned at any time during my meal, the fine print gives them the right to kick me out of the table but they didn't want anyone to know about it, such a dishonest practice. I wrote them back saying that it was wrong to not mention about the time limit at all in the restaurant and 1.5 hours was too short as I had to wait for the food to come in multiple rounds and they were slow since the restaurant was full on a Friday night; they made me wait for the food and they still enforced their time limit on my table. Also, the manager had "ordered" us to leave, instead the manager should have "asked" in a polite manner like in a "proper" Michelin starred restaurant. And then they just stopped communicating.
Tried the lunch ah ma kase, get to try eleven dishes mostly tasting portion. Food is good and it’s a good experience but I’ll prefer their alacarte order more as most signature dishes are there.

Peranakan dishes are rich and vibrant in flavor. I enjoyed the a-ma-kase dinner and almost got overwhelmed when they put out the main course consisting of five to six bowls. The desserts may need a little elevation.
第一次食娘惹菜，感覺幾有趣。食物擺盤都非常精緻，環境更加係無得彈。餐廳位處喺山上面，隔走咗大部分遊客，係一個好舒服嘅地方。

Had a great bday dinner in candlenut. Price reasonable food authentic and service by UNCLE FELIX-energetic and motivated man👍👏🏻we shall be back again.
GBU

Candlenut offers refined Peranakan cuisine with a modern touch. The tasting menu showcases bold, authentic Nyonya flavors while maintaining elegant presentation. Some dishes stand out more than others, but overall quality is consistent. Service is professional and informative. Slightly pricey, yet worth trying for a contemporary take on traditional heritage dishes.
Authentic nonya food.  Good environment.

Outstanding food in a Michelin starred restaurant serving Petanakan food with a modern twist. Service was also friendly,helpful and attentive.
Definitely deserving of Michelin star

A fantastic dining experience that is well worth the price! We had the 'ah-ma-kase' menu, and every dish perfectly balanced authentic local flavors with a fine dining touch. Even if you are sensitive to the strong shrimp and crab flavors often found in Southeast Asian food, the dishes here are very approachable without compromising on their unique local character.
Loved seeing a dining room full of locals—always a good sign! Make sure to leave some time to explore the area afterward; the neighboring clothing boutique and supermarket are super unique and great for browsing. A highly recommended spot!

Had a business meeting dinner at Candlenut. The food is great, good variety of local dishes. The service was a bit slow and didn’t hear quite clearly the introductions of some dishes.

Will probably come back for food.

Candlenut is a well-known restaurant serving refined Peranakan cuisine with modern presentation. The dishes are rich in traditional flavors while maintaining a fine dining touch. The ambiance is elegant yet comfortable, and service is attentive. It’s a great place to experience authentic Nyonya food in a premium setting.

My husband and I visit this one Michelin star restaurant two to three times a year. Really love their Peranakan food and the warm, friendly staff. And please order extra serving of chendol as most of the time this dessert is not on their ah-ma-kase menu but I will add it is a must-have.

ランチで訪問。テイスティングコースの 「ah-ma-kase」 を注文した。前菜3品から始まり、スープを挟んでメイン5品、最後にデザート2品がまとめて出てくる大皿取り分けスタイル。

これまで各地で、コンテンポラリー・アジアンをいくつも食べ歩いてきたが、その文脈で見ても、このコースはかなり楽しめた。コース全体を通じて、プラナカン料理の定番をモダナイズされたスタイルで楽しめる。良くも悪くも、小難しい蘊蓄やナラティブは介在しない。

メイン料理まで含めてすべて平らげたところ、年配のスタッフの方に「すごいね〜」と声をかけられた。中華圏では少し残すのが美徳、という文化的背景を踏まえると、これは一種の京しぐさだったのかもしれない。しかし、料理のボリューム自体はそれほど大きくはないので、無思考で食べ進めれば多分完食する。

感覚的に、プラナカン料理はワインとの相性があまり良くない気がするので、今回はハウスブランドのお茶で繋いだ。その選択は正しかったように思う。

なお、今回は腹ごしらえも兼ねて、リドリーパークのふもとから歩いてレストランを尋ねてみた。大豪邸や瀟洒な邸宅が立ち並ぶ品のいい散歩道なので、ルートとしておすすめしたい。

Had the Ah-ma kase for dinner and foood was really good! Well play of texture and taste!
It was super filling so pls come on a very empty stomach....

Service was amazing as well. They pay so much attention to details and take note on your pace of eating before serving the next course. 1 clear example was they noted I did not eat beef (because my partner ate both sticks) and offered me an extra pork one.
Only disappointed with the chendol I ordered.
mediocre

Mi aspettavo un ristorante diverso sia dal punto di vista del servizio, della mise en place, ma soprattutto delle pietanze proposte....sinceramente  ho trovato eccessivo l uso delle spezie che hanno coperto il gusto della carne! I vini sono eccessivamente cari! Peccato
Exquisite in ALL aspects. Tasting menue is outstanding.
Food was good but slightly on the milder side for Peranakan food. Was expecting more of a flavour bomb, but it felt like the spices and herbs were somewhat refrained.
I am asean but I feel the fine dining and peranakan cooking do clash. I will not go again. I did not take photos I had no interest in the platings as they were ordinary.

Celebrated my husband's dinner here and had the most amazing experience.
Food was excellent and service was beyond expectation.
Felix who attended to us was very attentive and provided excellent service.

Thank you for a wonderful experience

ランチコース(約13000円)は品数が多すぎです。半分も食べきれません。
なのでアラカルト2皿で十分です。
海老アレルギーがあるシンガポール人と日本人の複数メンバーで行きました。海老が入ったものは注文していません。他料理を食べても症状は起きなかったです。
誕生日はミニスイーツが提供されますが、正直その味は普通すぎました。味はほぼなくこの店にしては物足りないレベルでした。他店と比べて。
スープが美味しいです。ニョニャ料理は僕には辛すぎたので次回は注文しないです。
スタッフは丁寧でした
予約をしてなくても運良く入れましたが、平日でも満席傾向。行く前にのオンライン予約では空席あったんですが当日の営業時間前に埋まってしまうようです。
Tried the Ah-Ma-Kase menu. Food was ok but service was sub-par. Some serving staff is arrogant which is unexpected for a restaurant like this.

My farewell party here was perfect♥️ My precious friends, the delicious food (I especially loved the Ngoh Hiang and Wing Bin Salad), and enjoying the beautiful interior with the friendly service made my day really unforgettable. The Korean message on the dessert touched my heart😭 it was such a thoughtful and memorable detail. I highly recommend Candlenut !!

Fantastic ah-ma-kase lunch with impeccable service! I was eager to discover Peranakan cuisine and was not disappointed. Fresh ingredients that were both new to me and familiar combined into well-executed dishes that were a pleasure in taste and texture.
I am glad to have chosen the tasting menu to experience the different dishes. I wasn't able to finish all of the dishes, but it was only to make sure I had room for all of the dishes. I was pleasantly surprised by a Welcome dessert plate as well!
If I return to Singapore, I will make this a stop to discover more of this cuisine!
Great place and service, interesting food but did not blow me away.

Had a wonderful experience at Candlenut. The Peranakan flavours were beautifully executed, with the kueh pie tee being light, crisp and addictive. The chicken curry was rich, fragrant and comforting, while the pomelo kerabu was a refreshing standout that balanced the meal perfectly.

Special mention to Uncle Felix for his warm hospitality, he was friendly, attentive, and took the time to explain each dish, which really elevated the dining experience. A great place for authentic Peranakan cuisine done right.

Service here is awesome. The staff are very attentive. They also take time to introduce you to what you are having. They can assist you in pairing your drink if required.

You must try their seaweed bread, a mix of savory and sweetness, that is very rare.
Great service and amazing food! Chef's talented conceptualisation and interpretation of his childhood memories into taste. Every bite was a discovery! We thoroughly enjoyed the experience.
Everything at this place is good. Chef and staff are very friendly. Food is excellent. They actually texted to confirm about your dietary restrictions there’s any. Highly recommended.

Echoing another review, the entrance is indeed hard to locate and lacks a proper sense of arrival. The décor also wasn’t quite as shown in the photos online; it felt rather plain during our visit, or perhaps the space was undergoing some form of renovation.

Indoor ambience-wise, we were honestly a little taken aback by the overall setup. It felt somewhat lacking compared to expectations and did not quite match the impression set online or the price point of the experience. The tables also looked rather makeshift, with tablecloths seemingly just placed over them, which unfortunately affected the overall setting.

The food honestly was truly well done. The lobster was perfectly cooked and flavourful with the rich sauce complementing it nicely, the winter melon soup delicate yet comforting, and the duck beautifully executed with balanced seasoning. The nori bread was also memorable, especially with its crunchy outer layer and rich pairing with the lobster sauce.

We also echo a prior comment that the wind-down towards closing can affect the atmosphere. We do note we take around 3 hours to complete the meal as we like to take our time to appreciate each dish and aren’t fast eaters. However, just a heads-up to folks like us to consider booking an earlier slot if you prefer to enjoy the full experience without the end-of-service transition.
The lunch set is best value for money. We are very happy with the food and service. Totally spot on for our taste. Thanks chef and FOH staff.

My husband and I celebrated our anniversary at CeSoir and had an amazing time. The food was absolutely delicious, clearly made by a very talented chef. Every dish was thoughtful and beautifully done. The service was warm, friendly, and attentive, which made the night feel extra special. We couldn’t have picked a better place to celebrate and will definitely be back with more friends and family!

We had an event at Ce Soir and the staff were very helpful and thoughtful through the whole process. The food was extraordinary and right up our asian tastebuds.

Truly a wonderful experience.

Had an enjoyable evening with the talented Chef Seth Lai with every dish being a big hit on our palates, menu comes in a scrap book with graphics and detailed description of each dish origins as well as influences. Notable dish include Wintermelon – Peanut, Zuwaigani and Cuttlefish a comforting Cantonese styled soup course prepared with pork broth and goes with heaps of snow crab. South-African Abalone – 5-Grains, Sakura Ebi, Cucumber
Inspired by Malaysian fried porridge, this aromatic rice dish is slow cooked over charcoal for 5 hours in housemade hoisin sauce, lots of textures culminating from this dish. Kaya misu dessert had a local spin on tiramisu and kaya

The menu prepared by Chef Seth is amazing.
The Malaysian inspired theme with a twist that brings about palatable chemistry within each bite.
No item is disappointing.
The service was so good, is truly a great experience dining here.
The 8 course menu takes about 2 hours to complete, so do take it slow and enjoy the session.

Came to celebrate Christmas Eve & saying the food was amazing feels like such an understatement. This has to be the most creative and interesting menu I've ever experienced in my life. Each dish is just so creative in terms of the taste profile, texture & how it all just comes together nicely eventhough it may sound like a strange mix.

It was really tough picking a favourite coz everything was that good. I thought one of the earlier dishes was my favourite, then the next one blows your mind & that'll be your next favourite...and the cycle repeats 🤣

I do feel that you have to be adventurous to try this place & if you're picky about food or aren't open to new flavours, this might not appeal to you. I had monk fish (I think!) liver & I loveeed it! Never would I thought I'd be scrapping the bottom for more fish liver... Chef Seth Lai balanced the flavours really well & the service was excellent! Every dish was explained to us & we were told how to eat them etc. Would definitely recommend this place for a nice meal.
Amazingly wonderful restaurant with impeccable flavor and presentation! worth every penny. highly recommend.

Excellent meal, really good hosting! Two thumbs up. The starters were fabulous and set the meal off to a great start. Hamachi had a lovely twist, mackerel with the assam sauce was surprisingly good.. And the kaya-misu divine...
Very intimate restaurant with great flavors! Reservation advised.

My family dinner at Ce Soir has gone down in our family history as one of the best meals we have ever had.

The entire experience was top notch. The food was creative, delicious tasting, and beautifully presented. Every single dish was wonderful and we can’t pick a favourite. The service was impeccable as well - everyone was so attentive and friendly. I’m still dreaming about this meal!

Amazing restaurant! As a Malaysian I can relate to story of each dish, and after the first bite I was already impressed. Told my friend this should be a Michelin star restaurant, and she told me to turn around where I saw it’s actually on the Michelin Bib Gourmand. The food was so impressive, even the bread, which I usually do not like to eat. Crispy on the outside, soft and fluffy on the inside 👌💯everything was impressive, thank you Chef Seth, and Xing Ying / XY!

Amazing food. Creative ingredient,. The appetizers were so well balanced. The main was insanely good. And dessert was so pleasant.
Amazing staff. Chef Seth is truly a master of his craft.

Everything here is meticulous!!!

I visit Singapore around three times a year and I have dined at quite a number of fine dining restaurants. I wish I could have discovered this amazing restaurant earlier!

When I first stepped in, I was intrigued by the beautifully designed booklet explaining each dish in detail. The chef creatively drew all dishes in a vivid manner and explained the rationale of designing each dish. We were reading along while enjoying the meal throughout the night. Lovely! :-) We are still keeping this booklet as a recollection of our beautiful memories at Ce Soir.

Every dish we had that night was extraordinarily delicious. Some dishes we particularly enjoyed were “Wintermelon”, “South African Abalone” and their signature seaweed bread (I had two full myself!)

We are going to miss our time here. This is going to be one of my must-visit restaurants I am in Singapore every time

Ce Soir definitely deserves to be recognized by more food lovers / Michelin inspectors. I believe It is just a matter of time before it becomes more popular!

Had a great time at Ce Soir to celebrate my hubby’s birthday! Special thanks to Chef Seth and the rest of the Ce Soir team for truly making it an extra special occasion for us. The service was so warm and friendly and the food was fantastic! ❤️

Love the food. Chef was really friendly. One missing star is because
The food portion is too small

We celebrated our anniversary here and it was magical! We were dazzled by the culinary talent and earnestness of Chef Seth Lai, complemented by the superb and attentive service of his wife. Every course, every dish was beautifully presented, and explained. Chef used high quality ingredients, and the tastes were sublimal. We enjoyed every morsel! My husband’s fav course was the African Abalone with rice, mine was the hot Winter Melon soup. We want to give Chef Lai and his team 7 stars, a star for each of the 7 course! May you always shine and flourish! We’ll be back definitely:))

I am loss for words for every dish they serve! It sooo good that my world went silent and I could not hear anything else except my own “umm”, savoring on the food. It’s out of this world!

I can continue to describe in details but shall not bore everyone.

On top of that, the service level by Xinyi is first class!! Super attentive to our needs and she seem to have planted a chip in my brain to know what I was thinking! Insane! 😃

And I love the ambience!! How they cleverly use lots of flowers but yet not too over. It takes the whole dining experience to another level 👍🏻

I am definitely going back AGAIN and VERY SOON! ❤️
Probably top 3 in my list of fine dining restaurants in Singapore food was amazing  and well executed

Food - generally good with some real standouts like the foi gras starter, wagyu beef ( but this ups the price considerably) and desserts. Visually pleasing too. Excellent service and a pleasant ambience

Wonderful experience!  Chanced upon Cesoir on a Tik-Tok posting. Decided to give it a try for my partner’s birthday. From start to finish, it was fantastic. Halfway through, my phone battery was low. One of their staff, XY heard and passed me her portable charger. After I drained her charger, she passed me another. Even handed my partner a blanket cos she was feeling rather cold. Food was absolute top-notch as well. Chef Lai served most of the dishes to us. Very well planned menu, and I love the Apollo inspired wafer! Will definitely head back again. Do keep up the good work!

In the past, I have made no secret of my skepticism toward the term “chef.” It is a title often bestowed too liberally, diluted by repetition and routine. But tonight, at Ce Soir Singapore, I encountered something far beyond the realm of culinary convention.

Seth is not a chef.

To call Seth a chef would be to call Da Vinci a painter, or Mozart a pianist. Technically accurate, yes, but woefully insufficient.

What unfolded before me was not a meal. It was a symphony of sensation, a choreography of flavor and form that defied expectation and redefined experience. Each dish was a brushstroke on a canvas I did not know existed. The textures whispered, the aromas sang, and the flavors, ah, the flavors, spoke in a language that bypassed the palate and went straight to the soul.

Seth does not cook. He conjures. He composes. He creates.

There is magic in his hands, and mystery in his mind. He is an artist of the highest order, and Ce Soir is his gallery. To dine here is not to eat, it is to witness.

Not everyone can become a great artist; but a great artist can come from anywhere. And tonight, I met one.

His name is Seth.

The food is excellent and truly lives up to the restaurant’s being in the Michelin guide, making it perfect for special occasions and celebrations. Always accept when they offer you another round of bread—it’s absolutely worth it.

A real hidden gem that away from distractions in a black and white enclave in a deeply forested greenery. The entrance was a magical walkway into a space filled with lush flora display.

You are greeted by a little exercise book with whimsical and cute drawings of Chef’s child-like memories detailing his love for his Malaysia hometown and Japan. The flavours are well layered and you will enjoy the artfully curated dishes.

We ordered the full run at $228

Our favourites:

Wintermelon Soup
Smoked Iberico pork that’s hidden in a soup stock that’s slowly brewed for 12 hours. There’s cuttlefish, crab and simmered in generous chunks of the winter melon. When you dip your spoon into the soup, it unveils the smokiness of the pork. What a wonderful feeling it is to savour this hearty soup.

Lobster
Grilled lobster with beetroot and spinach drizzled with foie gras sauce.

Signature seaweed bread
So good you can eat it on its own!
Soft and fluffy with a sweet glaze and seaweed in it. You want to leave some behind to mop up the Lobster dish.

Chef Seth is very soft spoken and he works hard to prep, cook and serve with pride. I believe he is onto something exceptional.

Looking forward to see his creations!

Chef Seth Lai's gastronomical excellence and his creative use of bold flavours truly made his every dish a remarkable masterpiece.

The flavours in his every single creation explodes in our mouth waking up senses that we never knew we had.

We had indulged the $228 Dinner menu.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: 店家想開店就開、想休息就休息。遠道來訪的請三思，本人來了三次都沒營業。

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: 050326 $7.40 / Sizes of $6 7 8 10 with Rice 40c 50c / Ordered the $7 meat ribs.... the meat is so tender n the portion is SO MUCH MEAT.  The soup is also very nice. Despite the long Q at 12.35pm, I was served by 1pm.  The ladies are all very friendly n cheerful. Will eat again,  that's for sure.   Eaten at a few different places  n this is the best so far.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: Value for money for the portion size. Nice chewy tripe and chunky pieces of meat. But the soup is terrible - very very very salty and has an unpleasant bitter taste (too much herbs). Chilli could have been better if they made it more tangy.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: This place serves easily the best Chinese Herbal Mutton soup in Singapore. I don’t feel thirsty after drinking the entire bowl of soup, including 1 more refills! My stomach remains warm and that is an indication that they put the right herbs to nourish the body.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: Herby and peppery soup, big portions. Picture is $6 meat+tripe with big rice

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: Soup is nice with a tinge of herbal taste. Mutton is not handy and is very tender. No wonder so many elders patronize this stall. Portion is huge. $9, alot of meat that is enough for 2. The only downside - soup is quite oily.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews:
Madam taking order Very Polite.
Opens 11am but queue formed as clearly as 10.30am. Taste good worth to try. But every item has price range $6to$10 not sure every increment of $1 includes additional of what ? 🤣

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews:
The soup is fantastic—a strong, comforting herbal base that warms you up immediately. The mutton is incredibly soft and tender, clearly cooked to perfection without any strong gamey taste.

What surprised me, given the intense demand, was the good service! The staff handles the crowd efficiently and politely.

Be warned: This place is insanely popular. Expect long queues as they open around 11:30 AM and often sell out completely by 1:00 PM! It's a race against the clock, but definitely worth the wait for this level of quality.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: Stall is run by mother and daughter both whom are very nice and friendly. Love the mutton soup as it is with strong herbal taste. Ordered 2 bowls at $7 and $10. Quantity of meat is generous and soup is refillable. Easily one of the most satisfying mutton soup I have tried.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: .. for the price point .. SHOULD TRY place .. may be among the best

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: The herbal kick hits you immediately. The soup tastes so homely and comforting, and the mutton was so tender it was falling off the bones. A must try indeed!

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews:
Been wanting to try this but didn’t until today because the queue was ok.
For those who do not like herb, you will find it too strong tasting. Meat is soft and soup goes well with rice.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews:
Stall is only open for 1-2 hours. Most of the time sold out in 1 hour or 1.5hours. Queue is mad long but moves pretty fast.

Probably the best mutton soup I’ve had. No strong smell of mutton, meat is super soft and soup is very flavorful. Must try! Please come the moment they open for business!

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: Queue was long but fast. Mutton was tender and fragrant. Soup is herbal based but not too overpowering. Overall big big recommend

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews:
Very delicious Chinese style mutton soup.
Be prepared to queue and you will be rewarded with a satisfying meal.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: Portion is big and soup is tasty

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews:
Mutton ribs soup ($10 + $0.40 for smaller bowl of rice) - Excellent. Tender, meaty, fatty. Herbal soup.

From earlier visits:
Mutton stomach and brains soup ($10 including rice) - Excellent. Fresh. Good portion of stomach and brain (both grey and white matter). Good herbal soup.
Mutton meat and ribs soup with rice - Herbal, slightly salty, slightly bitter soup like turtle soup. The meat was tender and boneless.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: An unmissable queue snakes towards this stall at peak lunch hours, with neighbourhood regulars and office crowds waiting to fill their stomachs with bowls of full-bodied, herbaceous Chinese mutton soup. Served with rice and topped with finely chopped fresh ginger and coriander, the tender lamb meat and innards are balanced with a hints of freshness with each bite and mouthful of sweet, flavourful broth.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews:
Mutton soup is one of my favourite soup dish and I have tried several famous herbal mutton soup stalls in Spore, and I have to say this is the BEST mutton soup in Spore. The meat is very tender, and the soup is super rich & thick with various herbs, orange peel, Chinese cooking wine n ginger.

Kudos to the lady boss, prices have not changed over the past 10 years 👏
Totally deserving of their Michelin Bib Gourmand award 👍👍👍

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews:
Delicious herbal mutton soup with fall off the bone tender meat. Has the $8 portion with rice and it filled me up completely. The soup is a little lighter than the Pasir Panjang or the beauty world ones, but packs an equal punch in terms of the mutton and herbal taste.

Strongly recommend for anyone needing a herbal boost!

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: Excellent lamb rib soup tender meat falls off bone.  10/10. $9 serving was generous.  Sold out by 1pm

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: Not quite a fan of mutton smell. This is quite ok. A lot old people eating. Feel bit like turtle soup but more salty. Soup 5/5. Rib, marrow and tendons 4-5/5. Cilantro and chilli sauce 5/5. Rice 2/5. Openings time abit limited though. Minus star. The after taste of mutton lingering not so pleasant though. And thirsty due to the saltiness.

Restaurant Name: Chai Chuan Tou Yang Rou Tang
Reviews: Still taste as good during their father time. Friendly and polite. The passion in their food is marvellous.

The soup is 👍
Consider cheap
Service great as fast for long Q.
Overall taste so so, personal preference.

First time here and I have great expectations because of their reputation. Char siew was nice with the right amount of fat and lean meat but not charred. Wanton was nicely shaped and packed with ingredients but someone forgot to salt it. Overall the noodle was a bit bland for me. Also you have to add your own chilli. Not sure if Chef Kang meant his version to be healthy but I prefer a stronger savoury taste.

Best WTN I have eaten so far. Char siew is succulent and flavorful, unlike those dry and striking red coloured ones that we always see in hawker centres.

Hip hip hooray! Burrrrp!

My wife and I were here today (25 January 2026) for brunch, and it has been a while since the last time that we were both here. Being a Sunday, the queue was long but it moved reasonably quick, thanks to the stall chef's taking several orders in advance and preparing them sort of in bulk. My wife and I ordered our usual: a "Noodle with Char Siew and Wanton" each - with the Wanton served in a separate bowl of soup. As always, the whole ensemble was very good - the "in bulk" preparation notwithstanding - with respect to the noodles, the black sauce, the Wantons, the soup and of course the Char Siew. Everything was very moreish, yummy and flavourful. Service here, despite the continuous stream of customers, was good - patient and friendly. The dining ambience was nice enough, considering the place was not air-conditioned - there was ample seating and fellow customers were prepared to share tables that were very big.

Tried Chef Kang’s Wanton Mee for the first time and I was pleasantly surprised. With their 2× Michelin Star awardee reputation, my expectations were pretty high, but they really delivered. I ordered the abalone char siew wanton mee and it was so yummy — the noodles were springy, the char siew was tender and flavourful, and the abalone made it feel extra special. 🤩

The wantons were really good too — plump, juicy, and packed with filling. Even the soup was super comforting and tasty, which tied everything together nicely. It felt like simple comfort food done really well. Definitely coming back again! Very pleased and satisfying ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

It’s a genuinely good plate of duck rice. The meat is tender, and the rice tastes like well-perfected glutinous rice—glistening with fragrant oil without being overly oily. The chilli isn’t the dry type; it’s slightly sweet and sour, which I actually prefer. Not spicy, just balanced. This is the kind of duck rice you can easily eat on a regular basis.

What’s sad is that ever since the “Exposing Michelin” saga on TikTok, people have become overly critical, almost as if they must prove whether a stall is Michelin-worthy. The moment someone puts on the “food critic” hat, their expectations shoot up to unreasonable levels—completely unfair to the hawkers. Can we honestly say this stall serves bad duck rice? Of course not. So why the negative reviews?

If you’re paying $200 per person for a fine-dining meal, by all means, scrutinise every detail. Expect perfection. That’s the price you pay. But this plate of duck rice costs less than $10. Is it fair to demand perfection from hawkers who are literally helping us keep food affordable?

Since when did serving decent, honest food become a crime worthy of harsh criticism? Some may argue that criticism pushes them to improve, but does it really? At the end of the day, there are real humans behind the stall—people with feelings and pride in their craft. If we were on the receiving end of these unreasonable comments, would we feel we deserved it?

Sometimes, being decent is more than enough. And sometimes, appreciation goes further than criticism ever could.

A couple of small cons: the restaurant is cosy and can feel a bit tight when it’s packed, and the carpark is really dark at night — something to take note of

Overall, though, Claudine is excellent French dining done right. Would gladly return

Few restaurants in Singapore manage to feel both deeply personal and wildly imaginative at the same time, but this one does exactly that.

The restaurant reflects the background of Chef Rishi Naleendra, whose Sri Lankan heritage and Australian culinary training come together in a menu that feels expressive, thoughtful and constantly evolving. The tasting menu moves like a story, each course building gently on the last while introducing new flavours and textures.

Some dishes linger in memory long after the meal. A beautifully delicate Mud Crab Curry, inspired by Sri Lankan flavours, arrives rich yet elegant. The Aged Duck with Pepperberry brings deep savoury notes balanced by gentle spice. And the Caviar with Smoked Cream and Roti feels like a playful reinterpretation of familiar flavours elevated to something refined and luxurious.

Desserts continue the creativity. One memorable example is the Woodruff Ice Cream with Coconut and Pandan, a dish that feels both tropical and unexpectedly complex.

The room itself feels intimate and calm, allowing the focus to remain firmly on the food and the rhythm of the meal. Service moves with quiet confidence, guiding diners through each course without ever feeling formal or stiff.

What makes the experience special is that the creativity never feels forced. Every dish has a clear idea behind it, but the flavours remain comforting and deeply satisfying.

It is the kind of restaurant where you leave not just impressed, but inspired.

A place where storytelling, heritage and technique come together beautifully on the plate.

I’d seen Cloudstreet online many times, and it’s definitely one of the most talked-about two-Michelin-star restaurants in Singapore. The first floor is quite dark in style, while desserts are served upstairs — much brighter and better for photos. That said, the portions are extremely small, and the bread in particular has a strange texture, so most people (especially guys) are unlikely to leave feeling full.

The five amuse-bouches included: betel leaf with Australian oyster, beetroot with caviar, Scottish bamboo fungus, Jeju abalone with zucchini mousse, and white asparagus chawanmushi with oxtail consommé.
The abalone was boldly seasoned with a slight acidity, very appetising; the oxtail consommé had a silky egg and crisp white asparagus — the two most memorable bites.

The first course was Spanish mackerel, though it was introduced as horse mackerel. The fish was crisp-tender, paired with shiso, ginger, and sake — though the ginger was a bit strong.
The Australian freshwater marron was sweet and fresh, but the millet was overly salty. It came with a Southeast Asian–style lemongrass broth, fragrant with spices.

Next was French sea bass with crab roe sauce — the sauce was rich and umami, the fish skin perfectly crisp, and the flesh firm yet delicate.
The beeswax-aged pigeon was also excellent: aromatic sauce, tender meat, and easily one of the best pigeons I’ve had recently.

A Sri Lankan stout bread was served mid-meal — very sticky topping, dense and gummy texture, not particularly pleasant.
The main course was A4 wagyu from Tochigi with a wasabi-yogurt sauce. The beef was rich and buttery, while the wasabi sauce added freshness and balance.
At this point, I was only about half full when they told us to head upstairs for dessert — genuinely surprising.

The palate cleanser was a citrus granita with salt-baked marshmallow — slightly scratchy on the throat and not very suitable as a palate cleanser.
The first dessert was a black olive mousse, smooth and creamy, paired with a sweet strawberry ice cream — a good combination.

The main dessert was an artichoke ice cream with white crispy shards that were oddly hard; the mix of fruit and chocolate notes lacked a clear centerpiece.
Since I noted in advance that it was for 5/20, the restaurant gifted us a coconut cake — soft, fragrant, and creamy. Honestly, this could have been a better main dessert.

The petit four included: Australian wine-yeast ice cream with mild saltiness and alcohol notes; Sri Lankan palm-sugar profiterole filled with strong coffee aroma; and a hazelnut financier that was lightly sweet, soft, and gently nutty.

Overall, the experience — service, atmosphere, and ritual — was enjoyable, but the desserts were weaker and portions quite small. It’s a place worth experiencing once, though not one I would return to. Still, if you’re visiting Singapore, it may be worth a try.

Total: S$975.99 / 2 people
Rating: 7.5/10
Beautiful setting, grwat service and beautiful delicious food.
Loved the unique flavours, some with a hint of Sri Lankan touch. Every dish was well executed, and the service was warm and knowledgeable — a truly wonderful experience.

This place is definitely worth a detour! It provided an exquisite culinary experience that I would not hesitate to recommend. I dined at a dimly lit first floor where the snacks and non-dessert courses were served and was being escorted to a brighter lit second floor for the dessert courses and reminiscent about the succulent wagyu beef and the sweet blue lobster. While sipping my Pekoe Ceylon tea I secretly wished that the white pepper ice cream would one day rise to be the main dessert.

Thanks to the attentive, polite and professional waiting staffs, it’s a delight to know your dishes better and understand what the chef wanted the diners to experience. They were also quick to point up uneven grounds and steps while escorting to my seat or to the toilet. I felt the single glass wines were a tad expensive but I had one that paired well with my dishes.

잼나는 재료와 각국의 문화의 느낌있는 요리 굿 요기
시간이 조금 마니 걸리는게 단점

The service was so warm, personable!

First segment were Snacks:

Grilled Oyster, Coconut, Finger Lime
The oyster was wrapped in a betel leaf. Best eaten in one shooter, so that all the flavours and textures go well together. The finger like pops in your mouth.

Bergamot Meringue, Beetroot, Mandarin Kosho, N25 Oscietra Caviar
The meringue melts in your mouthm the sweetness, tanginess and saltiness umami from the beetroot, Mandarin and caviar blends well together.

Butternut Squash, Japanese Squid, Côm Rice, Fermented Chilli
The com rice is a nice crunch, the chilli hits you subtlety at the back palette. The grilled squid is grilled to perfection, smells so good and not too hard\overcooked nor undercooked.

Green Lip Abalone, Basil, Edamame, Zucchini
Our favourite was the abalone! It was surprisingly very soft, not chewy. The zucchini foam and basil oil made the flavours pop.

Celeriac Custard. Crab Consommé. Chilli
The crab consomme carries the flavour of the sea and so satisfying to savour it in your mouth (don't swallow it immediately!) can't really taste the celeriac tho, maybe the crab overpowered it.

Second segment was Seafood and Meats:

Carabinero Prawns, Chitose Tomato, Fermented Mango with Dill oil, N25 Caviar
The prawns were so succulent! The sweet tomato, tanginess of the fermented mango and brightness of dill oil, goes so well together!

Sri Lankan Curry of Western Australian Marron Aromatic Coconut Broth
Oh this was soo good! The millet porridge at the bottom is so well spiced! And coconut broth that is like red curry is so fragrant, warm and comforting! The server offered us a second helping of the broth that we gladly accepted.

Murray Cod, Fermented Bell Pepper, Almond
The skin is so crispy and fragrant! The spicy sauce had such nice dept.

Beeswaxed Aged Pigeon, Figs & Endive, Madeira Jus
The figs had sausage stuffing, made from the rest of the pigeon so the bird is not wasted. The meat was not too gamey, the fig jam was punchy

Sri Lankan Stout and Liquorice Bread
Another of my favourite! The bread was glazed with molasses. The bread was made with rye flour and soda. It was so fragrant! And so flavourful. The server offered us a second helping, totally enjoyed it.

Tochigi A4 Wagyu, Bell Pepper, Fermented Soy
Lamb neck at the side with pistachio crunch, with pistachio sauce, and fried kale chips and lamb jus
The pistachio crumbs and sauce was very creative. The lamb is so perfectly cooked!

Last segment was Desserts:

We headed upstairs. The ambience was so relaxing especially with the natural light coming in.

Pink Guava Sorbet, Rose Apple, Yogurt Marshmallow
Nice palate cleanser. The sorbet goes very well with the marshmallow. The sorbet looked like a tiny amount but the guava flavour was so intense.

White Pepper Ice Cream, Cherry Compote, Pecan, Candy Floss
This is such a fun dessert! The candy floss melts in your mouth. The white pepper is quite strong but in a good way. It gave the dish a smoky flavour. Pecans added a good crunch.

Cauliflower Ice Cream, Toffee Cream Cheese, Date Jam, Walnuts
The cauliflower crisps were so well made, they were baked at different temperatures to give it different colours.
There were Kueh lapis bits too!

The birthday cake (coconut cube) so so cute with the Playmobil man holding the candle!

Bread and Butter Pudding, Vegemite, Caramel
Interesting take on Vegemite on toast. So smooth!

Ragi Financier, Hazelnut Chantilly
Ragi was Sei Lankan millet I think. Interesting pattern on the top too

Coffee & Kithul Choux Puff
Kithul is Sei Lankan version of Gula Melaka. Pity this is the last dish!

Cloudstreet 🌟🌟 superb dining experience, everything just ON POINT, making me feel like a princess today. It’s one of the best Michelin I had visited (much better than one of the 3 stars Michelin in Singapore), will definitely visit again. Thanks Winnie for the amazing services ♥️

This is another restaurant in Singapore that is worth trying more than the local Michelin-starred ones. The overall taste is dominated by sourness. The oysters at the beginning are fresh and sweet, and pair perfectly with the 2008 Dom Pérignon. The red prawns are tender and go well with the sweet and sour sauce. The abalone with green edges, paired with edamame and the aroma of basil, is a seemingly simple yet not-so-simple dish that is truly excellent. The blue lobster with Sri Lankan curry and millet is unique, and when paired with the hot winter melon tea, the flavor is full-bodied. The cod was not particularly impressive to me; its freshness was not obvious, and the skin was hard to cut, but the texture of the fish meat was acceptable. Among the three seafood dishes, I think these best represent the flavors this restaurant intends to convey. The meat main courses are good, but I didn't feel they had any distinctive features. The pigeon meat with figs is similar to the flavor of duck meat with pears. Leaving aside the expression of Sri Lankan charm, I think it's a perfect dish. The wagyu beef is of high quality, but it's just wagyu beef. The bread and desserts in this restaurant are a major highlight. When I was offered a second slice and asked if I wanted more, I felt a sense of regret for not being able to eat more. The white pepper ice cream and cauliflower ice cream, with their salty and sweet combination, and enjoying the desserts on the second floor alone, all demonstrate the restaurant's confidence. At 398 per person for an 8-course meal, the wine list took me a long time to look through, and I didn't find anything I was particularly interested in. I initially wanted to go for Krug, but only the 2008 Dom was available, at 128 per glass. There might be better options.
Food is consistently excellent. If you like meat that is cooked more towards the well done end of the spectrum, make sure you let them know.

Was surprised to be seated at a long table facing the kitchen but it turned out great as the hosts were great conversationalists and the working chefs are a visual treat. Loved everything that we tried.

Moved up to another room for desserts and petit fours. The decor and furniture really put us into the mood for sweets even though there was no more space in our tummies!

All in all, an enjoyable 5-star experience. Worth coming for special occasions.

What began as an accidental booking at Cloudstreet turned into a rewarding dining experience. Unable to cancel at the last minute, I was impressed by how graciously the restaurant accommodated a same-day change of date.

This visit surpassed my previous one by far. Whereas my earlier dinner extended over four hours and left me somewhat restless, the lunch seating proved to be perfectly measured at two hours. That shorter pacing created the ideal balance, allowing the creativity of the chef’s compositions and the clarity of flavours to shine through.

Ultimately, what seemed like a mishap revealed itself as a reminder of how the rhythm of a meal can transform one’s appreciation of fine dining.

An unforgettable dining experience! Every course was beautifully presented and full of unique flavors. The service was warm and attentive, and the atmosphere felt both elegant and welcoming. Perfect for a special night out in Singapore.
Truly a special experience. Everything was well thought out and executed. Highly recommended

This is an Indonesian restaurant located along Tras Street. They were previously located along Tanjong Pagar Road.

The restaurant has been awarded the Michelin Bib Gourmand award annually since 2022, with the latest award on 2025.

The decor is very cosy, with Indonesian decor, batik tablecloth-covered tables and warm lights.

We ordered the following items:
- Sambal: Sambal dip to pair with your food. Spiciness level: 7/10.

- Nasi Kuning: This was tasty on its own and went well with the dishes. We couldn’t  stop refilling our plates.

- Sate Madura: Javanese-style chicken satay. Thick chunks of chicken on a stick and grilled. As the meat is well seasoned and grilled, no sauce was needed. It was served without peanut sauce, like the local version. The meat was tasty, though a tad charred on the outside and dry on some parts.

- Terung Belado: Thick chunks of brinjal, served with sambal. I like eggplant/ brinjal, so this was good for me.

- Tauhu Telor: Egg omelette. This was just alright, although it was a signature item.

- Sop Buntut: Oxtail soup with potato chunks and sliced carrots. Soup was rich and delicious. Meat was soft and tender. Recommended!

- Ikan Pepes: Fish covered with a 18-spice paste, covered with banana leaves and grilled. This was done well and the spices that coated the fish was reminiscent of otah paste. It’s good! Recommended dish.

- Udang Serai: Prawns done Balinese style. Prawns were fresh and cooked perfectly. The gravy was good and I scooped it all up. 😍 This is a must-try!

- Sapi Rendang: Rendang style beef. The meat was flavorful and tasty!

- Ice Chendol: Shavings of ice with chendol and coconut milk. What I liked was the Gula Melaka shavings at the bottom of the dessert cup. It would be better if there was more coconut milk to make it taste better. The green chendol strips were a tad skinny and dry looking.

I also had a fresh coconut which was refreshing.

The lady restaurant owner is very friendly and spoke to us. She shared that they prepare their food using minimal oil and use herbs and fresh ingredients for their dishes, which you can taste.

Overall, the food quality is good.

We left the restaurant with full tummies and we were delighted with our meal.

Recommended! 😋👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻
I am not an expert of Indonesian cuisine but my dinner was definitely not up to the standard of a bib gourmand restaurant in Europe.

Went to eat with an ex-colleague at Cumi Bali. The food there was so-so only. We ate grilled cuttlefish, tahu tempeh, lady’s fingers in chilli, and bergedil (potato balls). The two bergedil served were sour and obviously spoilt. They then replaced them with new ones.
After our meal, we decided to have chendol, which turned out to be a bad choice. The palm sugar used in the chendol was not pre-mixed as it should have been. Instead, it tasted like shaved sugar.
Before making payment, I decided to ask for the halal certificate as it was not displayed at the premises. I checked with Mr Google, which stated that the restaurant serves halal food, but I could not see the certificate anywhere.
To my surprise, their halal certificate had expired. According to the lady boss, they are in the midst of renewing it, but they have failed the audits required to obtain the certificate.
I am wondering whether they can still be considered halal when their certificate is still in the process of renewal.

Cumi Bali is not just another restaurant — it's a living story of passion, sweat (I know this, I run a cafe), and love. And that story belongs to Fiona.

I have known her for more than 15 years. For decades, she has been holding the torch of authentic Indonesian cooking, working day and night, 7 days a week, so that every plate carries the soul of tradition. That's not business — that's devotion.

When you eat here, you taste more than food.

You taste the flame of someone who refuses to compromise on authenticity.

The Michelin Guide has rightfully shone its light on Cumi Bali — the ultimate recognition of Fiona's dedication. But for those of us lucky enough to sit here, to taste and to feel her spirit in the food, we already know she is one of a kind. And so is the place; it really has some of the most iconic soundtracks (not recommended for a gym workout or cardio, for sure) and unmistakably Indonesian design inside. It works for some and doesn't for others, haha!

Fiona, you remind us all that food is heritage, food is family, and food is love. Respect.

The restaurant no longer serves nasi padang meals for one person.

had a brunch here based on an acquaintance recommendation, its such a hidden gem for an Indonesian cuision🤍
all the food we ordered were the best. definitely to come back and try out another dishes.
we had ayam goreng, daging rendang, sambal tauhu tempe, ikan kunyit and sambal terung😍
the staff (Fian) had assisted us very warmly and inviting🙏🏻

thank you and wait for our return in near future!🫰🏻
Slightly expensive because of the location; we enjoyed the food. Beef randeng is the way to go.
nice lah

ミシュラン1つ星。
マリーナベイサンズにあります。
落ち着いた雰囲気でゆったり美味しいお肉をいただきました。
サイドは量がとても多く4.5人くらいでシェアできると思います。ステーキをたくさんいただきたいならサイドは控えめに。
牡蠣や海老の海鮮料理もとっても手が込んでいて素晴らしかったです。
写真は食事に夢中で撮り忘れました。
Great food and even better service by Rjoy and Chai

Having reviewed the standard menu items previously, I’m focusing more on the off menu and seasonal specials.

From the seasonal specials, we had the roasted conference pear with burrata cheese. I love the pear , which gives the sweetness to the prosciutto crisps and the burrata cheese gives the creamy taste which was not cloying. The hamachi and scallop ceviche was also on point with its citrusy and salty flavours.

We had the off menu order of mushroom soup and lobster bisque. Both were decent,  not overly rich, though the mushroom soup was on the saltier side.

The prime porterhouse steak and pork chop kept to their usual standards. It was the first time we tried the rotisserie chicken which was tender and flavourful. Another first was the lamb chops which was well marinated and easy to chew. Another off menu was the Shanghai lobster curry rice, which was presented nicely with the lobster shell and chopped meat drizzled with curry on rice.  Slightly on the sweeter side but something different from the standard menu.

We had the standard signature sides of peewee potatoes, creamed spinach, sautéed mushrooms, mash potatoes and my favourite was the roasted broccoli.

Of the 3 desserts of strawberry almond financier, chocolate soufflé, baked Kaya Alaska, the last with my favourite Kaya was to my liking.

Oh other than the signature ‘Call Me Daddy’ cocktail, we tried a variety of mocktails, mainly fruity floral and all looked and tasted good.

The food was too expensive.
No other complaints about their roasted veggies and steak. I love crispy medium rare steaks.
Roasted brussel sprouts came with guanciale I think? Very nice!
Went on Valentine's day. My wife and I enjoyed a lot!

We celebrated my birthday at CUT by Wolfgang Puck and it was truly an unforgettable experience from start to finish.

First, the service was exceptional, warm, attentive, and incredibly thoughtful.

The steak was absolutely fantastic, perfectly cooked with a beautiful crust on the outside and tender, juicy inside. Easily one of the best steaks I’ve had in Singapore. And I have to specifically mention the mashed potato,  hands down the best I’ve ever tasted. Silky, buttery, and impossibly smooth. It deserves its own spotlight.

We were also pleasantly surprised with complimentary sliders and sweets, which were such a lovely touch. The birthday dessert plate was beautifully presented and made the evening feel even more special.

The ambience is elegant yet comfortable — perfect for a celebration or a special night out.

Highly recommend for anyone looking for a top-tier steakhouse experience in Singapore. I’ll definitely be back. 💛

Pleasant experience at the Cut. From the bread basket, cocktails, starters, main course (steak of course) to desserts and the coffee, the food was excellent. My husband and I had a wonderful time, thanks to Steven who was attentive and knowledgeable. Will definitely be back again:)

The best CUT branch i came to, am at the top of the satisfaction level from the full experience, food, service atmosphere and all

No wonder they have a michelin star

Special thanks to Rjoy shes the best

Definitely will come back during our next visit to Singapore

Overall, was a pleasant 1st dining experience at Cut tonight.  We were served by Kay who was very attentive and took very good care of our needs.  We had the early cut menu and ordered a half-bottled of wine.  The quality of food was generally great (the oysters and crab cake was good, the sirloin was cooked just right, apple crumble was very delicious and almond financier, though didn’t look like a financier but good.

The only complaint we had was the lobster was too overcooked, so we gave feedback to the chef but rather than an apology for an overcooked lobster, I was told that the chef still insisted that the lobster was cooked nicely. Trust me, as it is one of my favourite dishes, though it was consumable, I can certainly tell what it means when the lobster is stringy and chewy… Regardless, I think the restaurant handled it well by extending a nice gesture with regards to our feedback.

Just wondering, when there is a quality issue and yet the cook (I wasn’t sure where it was a senior chef or junior chef who replied) insisted otherwise, it prompted us to wonder if the person who cooked the dish could really tell when the lobster was overcooked or not and to me, that will be of a greater concern.

In short, I will likely dine there again, but unlikely to add lobster next time.

Celebrated my fiancé’s birthday at CUT because he has always wanted to try the steakhouse. They did not disappoint.

The service was impeccable from the moment we entered. The porterhouse was perfect (although I think we ordered a bit too much for 2), first time trying the crabcake and it was so delicious, think it’s going to be something I’ll crave for from time to time.

Last but not least, I got my fiancé an Omega watch for his birthday and as a wedding gift as well. When one of the service crew saw, he came over and congratulated us. While I was contemplating what to have for desserts because I was too full, he mentioned because I gifted my fiancé a watch, he will in return gift me the dessert (I thought he was joking) just that he’ll be making the choice for me instead.

The chocolate soufflé was sooooo decadent. It’s soft, it’s rich but it’s also light, I’m not even sure if I’m making sense here but yes.

In the end when we paid for the meal, I noticed that the dessert was really on the house. So thankful for the wonderful experience and I hope to go back again when we are officially wed this summer :)

果然是新加坡必吃牛排(  ᵒ̴̶̷᷄꒳ᵒ̴̶̷᷅  )
蟹餅no.1

📷Foodie Insta & Threads: @notso_foodie_travel
Love the experience and place

We had a birthday celebration at Cut by Wolfgang Puck, and the experience was truly unforgettable. The food was amazing—especially the fillet mignon and asparagus, which weren’t even on the menu and were specially prepared by the chef. A big thank you to the chef, because it absolutely blew my mind.

What really made the night exceptional, though, was the service. I’d like to highlight Dan and Kay Enn for their outstanding hospitality. I was dining with my two kids, and my younger one (4 years old) can be quite difficult to manage. She became upset and kept crying while blowing the birthday candles, but Kay Enn was incredibly patient and attentive. She went above and beyond to calm her down by offering a complimentary ice cream, which we truly appreciated.

Dan was equally impressive. He made the effort to remember our names and addressed us personally instead of generically calling out to my husband. That small but thoughtful gesture brought the service to an entirely different level and made us feel genuinely valued.

Amazing food, amazing staff, amazing service, and a wonderful environment. Absolutely worth paying for a premium dining experience. We will definitely remember this night.

Thanks to Ms Vatsala Rjoy she truly fantastic. All her introductions menus are out of heaven. Without her without quality service of CUT. Thank you. We had a great time and the restaurant does deserve michelin star.
Excellent food and perfectly cooked steak. Service was good, but the courses came out too fast. For a restaurant of this caliber, the experience felt rushed and should have lasted longer.

We had such an incredible experience and the food was next-level delicious! Despite not having had a booking, we were accommodated for straight away and given the upmost care by all of the staff!

Having multiple dietary requirements including being coeliac, the experience was beyond stress free, with the staff making me feel so comfortable and the chefs making changes to the menu to accomodate! The food was truly mouth watering! We couldn't be more appreciative!

A special mention to Rjoy and Vatsala who were so attentive, kind and made our experience one to remember! We will definitely be back in the future!

Tonight I went to enjoy a beautiful meal with my wife and thats what I got... We were greeted by a lady named Vatsala and she was amazing from start to finish I can't say more about her, she was the best so helpful amd truly knows how to look after the customers. It ia people like her thats the owners should really appreciate. I hope to come back soon and enjoy the quality of service I received tonight thank you again Vatsala and also R Joy

Very good food with very good service
Server: Vatsala and Arjoy

Had an early dinner at CUT by Wolfgang Puck, Singapore. Ordered the Filet Mignon, Baby Chicken, and Sirloin. While my medium‑rare Filet Mignon was slightly dry, the overall quality of the food was good and flavours were well executed. The Baby Chicken and Sirloin were enjoyable and nicely prepared.

Service was a little slow, but still acceptable and polite given the pace of the evening.

Overall, a pleasant dining experience for a refined steakhouse meal.

Many thanks to Hari and Stella for taking care of on our first trip to CUTS for our wedding 💍 anniversary!

Excellent steak, nicely cut and presented... The crab cakes were unusually good compared to any I've had before.

We were seated in a alcove so the noise wasn't too bad for us.

The restaurant presented us with a complimentary little cake and candle 🕯️ to celebrate our special day... Thanks again!

Came to CUT with my mum for my birthday dinner, and it was honestly such a memorable experience from start to finish. The service was amazing with Vatsala and Chariz, they were warm, attentive, and made the whole evening feel genuinely special without ever being overbearing. They checked in at all the right moments and were great with recommendations. I love that they started the meal with various types of bread as well for appetiser and i finished off with my favourite soufflé that they had.

A special shoutout as well to Chef Frederick, the food was outstanding and beautifully executed. Everything we had was cooked perfectly and paced well, which really elevated the night and made it a real special occasion.

If you’re looking for a place that delivers both exceptional service and a celebratory dining experience, I’d absolutely recommend CUT. Will definitely be back!

A disappointing first point of service interaction I experienced today while making an enquiry to change a table for a friend to CARMEL.
To be concise: the staff member I spoke with informed me—without any apology, or the basic courtesy expected in hospitality—that “7pm is full, not available.” The tone used was unfriendly, curt, and came across as condescending without offering alternative for example. When I asked for clarification regarding the tone, she immediately denied any issue in an equally dismissive manner.
For an establishment of CUT’s calibre, especially within Marina Bay Sands, such frontline behavior is extremely surprising and frankly unacceptable. This is not reflective of the service standards I have experienced during previous visits, which makes today’s interaction even more disappointing.
To be clear, I am not seeking any complimentary / compensation gestures or follow‑up calls. My intention is simply to highlight a very poor first point of contact that does not align with the reputation or expectations of a luxury dining venue.
We had our 10 year wedding anniversary at CUT. The best steakhouse in town!

We recently dined at CUT at Marina Bay, expecting a refined Michelin-star experience. While the food was excellent and met our expectations, the service unfortunately did not align with the restaurant’s reputation or pricing.

Our assigned waiter displayed a lack of attentiveness throughout the meal. Dishes were presented carelessly, water orders were mixed (still and sparkling), and there was unnecessary pressure placed on our group to order quickly. On several occasions, we had to request assistance from staff not responsible for our table, as our primary server was unresponsive.

Given the premium price point of approximately SGD 1,500 for four guests, the service fell well short of what one would expect from a fine-dining establishment of this caliber.

Came here to celebrate my fiance's birthday and I would like to thank the staff for their service. I was served by Roy and Tony and their service was excellent and truly professional. They were attentive and hospitable throughout the night and I would like to commend them.

Food was excellent and they have maintained their complimentary bread's standards over the years, which is truly heartening to see. Steak had a great crust and was tender, brussel sprouts were grilled nicely, and the Mac and cheese was amazing. The array of sauces served with their steak also works perfectly well.

Will highly recommend this restaurant to celebrate your special occasions.

This is the best curry chicken noodles that I have tried…hidden gem, better than all the stores in the well known hawker centre in Chinatown! The pig skin is an added bonus! I always order the large portion with thigh meat and add extra pig skin!

Curry was fragrant without being overly thick , chicken was super tender. The addition of pig skin here is a huge plus point compared to the Hong Lim stalls. Lady boss was very friendly , telling me their stall has been around for 40+ years and now is the second generation running the stall .

Best curry noodle in town.
I personally think it is better then China Town.
Aunty also super friendly!! But very warm.. omg

Good variety of food sold here and all are delicious! Great start to the Singapore chicken rice experience w fragrant rice, silly smooth poached chicken and spicy and tangy thick chilli sauce. Soup comes with generous topping of bean sprouts which is a plus for fibre intake. Owners are friendly as well and it's even at 3pm, there were still people coming for the chicken rice! Although the chicken rice is on a pricier side, don't be fooled by the high price because the portions and taste more than justifies for that!
The chicken is very smooth and the curry is very nice, especially the tau pok. Plus super friendly boss! Will definitely support!
Everything is perfect from chicken to rice to curry

Rarely met impolite Food sellers in Singapore and this is my second time. Although the food is good, but the aunty taking orders is very rude and not familiar with what they sell.When asked what is the diff between small and medium, she said is the same. Then I asked whether medium has added noodles or meats, she shows impatience and raised her voice , insisted is the same and shows bad attitude. So I ended up ordering the small one since she can't explain to me the diff between small and medium . Hello aunty you want to sell your food and can't explain your pricing well and yet show your impatience? You are Michelin starred doesn't mean you can be arrogant and show your attitude to customers
Extremely tender chicken with soup full of chicken liver + old cucumber taste and fresh vegetables. Rice and sauces are okok for me. Good portion and satisfying for just $5.

4 stars for the chicken rice which I think is of decent quality. Chicken is tender and rice is not broken. I didnt like the chilli though.

Curry chicken noodle which i tried years back, wasn't noteworthy. You probably get better versions at hong lim or bedok interchange.
The Hainanese chicken & rice of my dreams. You simply must try it for yourself. 10/10 would recommend.

The chicken rice is absolutely worth the queue and wait. Tried eating there before and today had takeaway. Both are equally delicious. The chicken is tender and juicy. The rice was also having just enough oil thus it’s not too dry or too oily. The chilli was also perfect as it further enhanced the flavour for both the chicken and the rice. All in all it’s definitely worth the try but to remember to queue early so as not to be disappointed for it being sold out!

The chicken rice is really good! The chicken is tender and juicy, and the rice is fragrant and flavorful. Chili sauce and soup go very well together. Portion is generous and worth the price. Will definitely come back again!

I can say it’s the best chicken rice in SG .

Curry noodle is nice. One of my favourite curry noodle store in town. Lady owner was friendly as well.

Unfortunately, had food poisoning after the last time. Maybe I was unlucky this time round 😭
love their curry soup great flavour and balance ！best in town！

Just landed from our flight and had the intention of going straight here for our first meal - was worried as it was half an hr before their google advertised closing time and arrived to see the owner washing up, we tentatively asked if we can still order and he warmly said yes and made us a chicken rice and chicken curry noodle.

The food was FANTASTIC - despite being the end of day portions the chicken rice had lots of flavour as well as being tender and the curry noodle brother was still RICH and tasty. The owner and his mother were very friendly talking to us, and giving us a free complimentary side soup which tasted great! We will definitely be returning before we leave based on the food and service!
Love love love the curry chicken noodles! Both Lao ban and auntie always so smiley and friendly too!!
10/10 would eat again. Chicken was so tender  and curry super fragrant. Owner was friendly too. There’s a coffee stall right behind them sells great coffee too.

Best chicken rice! No doubt!
Since my Secondary School days, i have been having this chicken rice whenever i visit army market for NCC.
Last time was the uncle and auntie, now is the younger generation liao… but taste is still same!
White chicken is soft, rice is fragrant… best!

Very good bowl of curry chicken noodles

The soup is very flavorful and esp so when you eat the soup soak taupok

Noodles portion abit small so recommend to add noodles if you’re a guy. Otherwise they do give quite alot of ingredients so $6 price tag not too bad

Ordered the chicken wing of which meat quite tender but can’t really taste the original taste since soak in curry

Good that no queue on wkday lunch though it’s good. Highly recommend

This is the first time I successfully ordered a chicken as they are usually sold out by early afternoon. This is definitely the top three chicken rice for me insofar the chicken rice I have eaten in recent memory. I am always marvelled by how tender the chicken is - even for parts like chicken breast which is usually tougher. For me, the rice either makes or breaks this dish - and the rice here is the type to die for - quality rice which is firm and aromatic. It’s one of those gem here in this food centre that is not to be missed.

Visited earlier this year. One of the best meals I ate this year. The curry chicken noodles were absolutely fantastic. Really delicious broth and lots of tasty ingredients. Had to queue for a while (weekday lunchtime) but was definitely worth the wait! Good value for money and friendly staff.

The owner was super nice. I arrived yesterday and went to his shop and he sold out. I returned the next morning...
He served me before the shop was open and even got us the curry noodles to try.
Thank you.

Located at a hawker center this place serves up a really good curry chicken noodle. It's spicy so be warned. Flavors were good, curry was rich but wasn't too thick. Chicken was tender and the dish came with Tau-pok or bean curd skin which soaks up the tasty curry. There was an addition that I haven't seen elsewhere, pork skin. Whilst it wasn't crispy as you'd expect, it added a unique taste to the dish, imagine pork crackling but soaked in curry, hard to explain but it had a unique soft texture. I ordered then smallest portion at 6 dollars and was thoroughly satisfied. They have another outlet at Tanglin Halt but everytime I go there, they are closed. This one is always open when I visit. Highly recommend this place if your craving something spicy!
Da Po Hainanese Chicken wins food bloggers with silky chicken, fragrant rice, punchy chili, and comforting old-school vibes. Simple, soulful flavors make every bite memorable and crave-worthy joy!!!

Very very juicy chicken meat, even when we got chicken breast (which can be dry), the breast meat from the shop remained juicy.
2 people serving is $12. There is a queue for this shop but worth queueing!

Generous portion of breast meat for the smallest chicken rice at $5. Chilli sauce was generous compared to many other stalls with lime juice in it. But meat was a bit dry for me despite adding dark soy sauce and chilli sauce. Guess it wasn't my day to get the meat with jelly under the skin.
Extra star for the food presentation despite takeaway.

Even for someone like me who doesn't have a high tolerance for spicy food, I really love their curry chicken noodles!

The soup is mildly spicy and has a fair bit of coconut milk so the taste and texture is good, then together with the chicken, noodles, potato, tau pok, and I think fish maw(?), it was a really good meal!

Visited on Nov 2025, not bad chicken rice at a corner of golden mile food centre. The portion are generous and service are good. The price is reasonable. Lots of people ordered the chicken curry noodles. Guess it's good, I order chicken rice. Not bad but not fantastic. Next round must try the noodles.
