Chicken rice $2.50. there is a bigger portion at $3 if you want more.
Roasted pork & char siew at $4
Been a regular at their store..Even price is higher alil nw but still worth it.
High CP value for a chicken rice in the neighbourhood least the queue. My go to chicken rice store whenever i am free.
Good chicken rice in the West . The price a bit steeper probably due to the ban of fresh chicken from Malaysia 😅

The rice of the chicken rice is superb. My kids after eating since young, now they are in the twenties still said best chicken rice.The cost of per plate of chicken rice was $2.50, just increased due to the lack of fresh chicken if not,  they have been selling $2 per plate.
One of the best chicken rice you can find in Singapore.

All time favourite. Best chicken rice in the west. Have been eating here for more than 10 years and never tired of it. Rice is tasty, chicken soft, don't even need to eat with chilli. Cheap as well. $2 for 1 packet of chicken rice, $11 for half a chicken and $22 for 1 whole chicken.

Hokkien Man Hokkien Mee is run by Xavier Neo, a former sous-chef at the Three Michelin Starred French restaurant Les Amis. He also gained experience at White Rabbit and Resorts World Sentosa. Xavier applies French culinary techniques to traditional Hokkien mee, such as preparing the prawn stock similarly to a lobster bisque, which enhances the depth and umami of the dish. Looking forward to eating on 15th March 2026.
Soupy broth style with a prawn taste.
Amazing food always

Solid Hokkien mee with a lot of Zhup (sauce) which I love. Not a very strong wokhey taste but still very flavourful.

We ordered a medium portion to share between two, came with four prawns and a few slices of abalone. We also added an omelette on top.

I’ve visited once before years back and it’s my second time giving them a go. Both times left good impressions.

It’s definitely on the pricier end for this local dish. Up to each diner to decide if it’s worth.

Ordered small $6 hkm. Pretty fast around 5min.

It's okay. The only wow part about this is how wet it is. Most wet hkm I have. Size is small for $6. But u will feel full due to the broth. Flavorful but not mind blowing zero wok hey.

Chili was meh no kick and relatively little. Lard was passable. Sotong was good.

Harmony wise I feel it has that hkm next door feel. Something I eaten when I was younger. Good for suddenly graving but not worth if u need to travel.
Taste was OK lah. Wok hei is too light.
I am impressed by the high quality of the hokkien Mee 👍👍👍👍👍👍👍

Price high, taste not even authentic hokkien mee taste. Disappointed with the taste even at first bite. Attitude was bad also, full of arrogance. Don't waste your time on this stall. So many other better hokkien mee than this.

The food is good — the prawns are fresh, and the abalone is also fresh. The ex-Michelin restaurant chef is definitely a highlight. There was no queue during lunchtime, so it was easy to get a seat. I think if they could offer more seasoning or sauces for free (instead of can’t), more customers would be happy to return for sure. Maybe this is a local style, but unfortunately I couldn’t fully enjoy my meal...

Ordered 18 bucks portion they gave 3 small plates
Asked for one more small plate and was asked to fork out more money for it
Sure we are all struggling with increase in prices. I don't think this was unreasonable.
But sure it's your business you run it your way

Price at $6.50 for small but quantity is still quite big
Prawns is big and fresh
Comes with abalone
No pork lard, sambal chili instead of belacan. Very strong wok hei flavour
Heard it's Michelin standard so gave it a try overall is not bad, definitely above average but nothing exceptional
Good hkm, a bit pricey

Very very disappointed & waste money ($6.50).  No wok-hey, chilli no fragrant, so little & not spicy all all. Other places $5.00 much better.
1st try also the last try for me.

I must say the broth used is good. Garlicky and fragrant. However, i would prefer more wok hei. But this is just my personal preference. At $6.50, it is not as affordable as most but given that it is cooked well, it was still a good eat.

I have ate at this stall many times. Never failed to impress me with the strong flavourable taste until three weeks ago. The standard has dropped so much and the taste is just above average. No longer as good as it used to be. Moreover, no sotong and the price is on the high $6.50.

Nice Hokkien mee.
More to the pricey side but I am willing to pay for the extra egg!

Taste okay, but lack of wok-hey. Not cheap as the $6 portion is quite small. Ordered a plate $6 and a plate of $10 for comparison. Chilli given too little, but dare not ask for more as hawker charge extra. Pork lard could be better if serve by placing at the side instead of mixing it together when cooking.

Ordered by delivery platform.
1st off,i must say i am not concerned in the keast if the chef is ex les amis or my friend's neighbours uncle's cousin. Long as he whips up a mean plate of HKM,that is what matters the most.
And a mean hokkien mee,it really is. The fried mee is fully submerged in the broth, and oh my,the broth is indeed heavenly.
Wok hei in this case is subtle, but the broth more than makes up for it. It is full of umami, and I couldnt resist slurping down the lasr remnants of it. Chilli given was sufficient,not a whole lot,but definitely enough for 1 pax.
If u prefer your HKM dry and chillified, this HKM is not you. In my case,i like both versions so I am a happy camper indeed.
Paid $10.40 sans delivery fees for a 1 pax meal. Will definitely buy again.

They don’t serve lard. That’s a huge minus for me. But the noodles were tasty and there was a wok hay. The gravy was decent too. They serve some fake abalone slice instead of the usual seafood. It’s decent but I won’t go out of my way to eat it.
GRRRROOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSSSSSS!!!!
Taste ok, but prawn not clean.
Decent plate of hokkien Mee, nothing much to shout about

Hokkien man, hokkien mee. What a nice rhyming stall name.

Located at a coffeeshop Blk 19 Toa Payoh Lor 7, is the workplace of Mr and Mrs Xavier Neo. Before setting up his stall at Toa Payoh, ￼Mr Neo was the chef of michelin 3 stars restaurant Les Amis.

So how good is his hokkien mee? Is it the best ever? I immediately ordered my food and was given a buzzer. Found a seat and waited for it patiently. Not too long later, the buzzer vibrated. Yay finally my food is ready.

I have high expectations for it since it came from a sous chef. The presentation of the dish is already nice. Nice plate unlike the common kind we found at the famous stalls. One thing caught my eyes, the prawns. It looks like they came directly from the ocean. Wow i cant wait.

Lime is a must. Thankfully they gave me one so i gladly squeezed them unto my food and gave it a good stir. Time to dig in!

Oh my gosh. The food is soooooo awesome. I kid you not, the broth was well soaked by the noodles, making every mouth of the mee taste so umami. It’s sweet and savory at the same time, something i didn’t expect hkm to taste so good. The eggs go so well with the hkm but the best of them all is probably the prawns. As good as it looked, it tastes amazingly fresh. For a hawker dish below $10 i think this is really worth it. 一分钱一分货, i am in love with this hkm.

This is one of my 2 favourite hkm in the world. If you have not tried this before, go and try it. No need to quote sek fan lo! Fb grp because there wont be any discount.

I love this and i will go back again and again.

#hkm

The taste of this Hokkien mee standard had drop compare to previously they cook.
Price is high and definitely not worth to order.

No fry pork oil sold anymore, lost the traditional taste of Hokkien mee. 2 Star it’s only for the egg is nice only
We ordered the $12 one. The Hokkien Mee lacks wok hey, but tastes pleasant. Good to try when you happen to be in the area.
Should cut down on the noodles and add at le last 2 more prawns.
Nice flavor and fresh ingredients, can have more wokhei. Quite garlicky. Slightly pricey
Satisfying plate of Hokkien Mee , Would say its 3.5/ rather . Not top tier for me but better than average

Easily the top 3 Hokkien Mee of you like the wet type. The broth is incredibly flavorful with a good umami kick. Noodle is firm and Al-dente. The squid deserves a special shout-out. It was so soft and almost abalone like. Well done!
位置在一楼很好找，楼上应该是居民楼吧。肉骨茶很好吃，5新那份就能吃饱。
Rather uncommon, the soup is really dark with slight hints of herbal notes. Meat cuts were decent.

Good value for money. Their bak kut teh has a super dark brown broth, with a strong Chinese herbal medicine flavor (people say it's the Malaysian style), so it's not the kind of typical Singaporean bak kut teh with dominating peppery taste. I prefer the Singaporean style, so I'll take a star off the rating but it's just a matter of personal preferences.
Love the steam fishes

Bak kut teh ($9 for long ribs + $0.50 for rice) - Excellent. Large, tender and meaty. Came with 3 ribs.

From earlier visits:
Bak kut teh ($9 for long ribs) - The 3 long ribs were fairly tender and easy off the bones.
Bak kut teh ($8 for large portion) - There were 3 long ribs and 1 short rib. Quite meaty and tender. Strong herbal flavour from the broth.
Large intestines (大肠) ($5) - Good.
Yam rice ($0.70) - Not bad but could be warmer.
针不挫，好吃😋

Few days ago, I was eating the Pork Trotters at the corner stall called Morning Bak Kut Teh.

In terms of soup, Morning BKT is better. More herbaceous.

In terms of portion, I would say Hokkien Street uses better quality.

In terms of Service, go to Morning BKT if u like to be shouted at.

Cleaninliess?   AVOID attempting to self self with the cut chillis.  I got a huge shock when I see how dirty the spoon was.  It appears that it hasn't been washed for many yrs. The chillis also looked decomposed and discoloured.

Overall, I will choose Hokkien Street BKT.
Decent bowl . Meat was soft but found the soup lacking flavor
good

早上8.05am 来叫一份小的猪脚和我说还没好 但是大份的就有 问我6块的行吗 ，一个人吃不了那么多 就换了个肉骨茶肉丸汤 结果和我说还没好 时间还很早，不好意思

结果8.10am 有位顾客来了 叫了份肉骨茶 很神奇竟然开始卖了，不想做小份的生意 可以直接把价格全部换去高的 或者直接个附加条件下去~
都不知道怎样做生意的 8点还说太早 还没营业就一开始说就行了~
Meat was extremely tender, worthy of their michelin
I found the soup to be quite bland. I tried another Bak Kut Teh stall at the corner, and it suited my taste better, perhaps because their soup is more flavorful, along with the braised sauce.
We woke up early and there wasn’t too many places open. Glad this was open. The herbal ribs was very tasty. Fragrant! $6 can’t be beat!

I ordered the long rip BKT for 6sgd and rice . It's a good portion for the price. The meat is super tender and tasty, the soup has a bit of a bitter note. Could be more herbal for my taste, but overall a solid old style BKT. Service straight forward and friendly. Recommended!

Awfully bad. Asked for 2nd top-up soup and they were very stingy with the amount and filled up with 1/4 portion 🥲 And my daughter tryna ask for another top-up because it was extremely less than we expected and all she got the response was “NO MORE SOUP” and the staffs are taking orders from the back. Oh wow fantastic. Why do business of BKT when you are so stingy…………
Extremely stuck up attitude. like owe the staff a living

Chance upon this since I'm in the vicinity. Didn't even realise there's a Michelin rated bak kut teh in this food ctr. And equally surprised is they're serving Hokkien style(dark colored broth) coz almost all Bak Kut Teh in SG are the clear peppery broth kind which is teochew style. But the spare rib is tender, braised trotter also tender and savory, boiled peanuts too done just nice, unlike another Michelin rated beef noodle I had yest in Taiwan whose peanuts were too raw, hard. And they also serve red cut chilli with thick dark sauce as dips, a welcome sight vs those bkt joints in MY all serving with the cheap green chilli padi.
Pathetic portions and not as tasty as before.
This is the comfort food since my childhood days. One of the most original BKT stall in Singapore. It's not Malaysian or Singapore styled, but old style.

Bought this bkt after seeing an ah mah eating.

1 bowl has 3 meaty ribs😚
Although not fall of the bone tender, the meat is not tough or dry. It has a nice bite to it!! The meat they use is fresh and good quality. Be sure to eat with the dark soya sauce;)

The flavour of the soup is just nice, not too herby👌 (so its not for someone who likes very herby bkt)
Although the soup looks abit oily, it is alright when you drink it.

This is a good bowl of bkt that I will return to eat! (It is goood but not wow
Đáng để thử

Great Bak Kut Teh stall that is located in Hong Lim Food Centre.

Do try their pig kidney soup.

My first visit to this stall and I ordered the pig trotters. The $6 portion was decent. What caught me by surprise was the meat came w/o the bone, which made it easier to eat.

OMG the skin and meat were so tender! Tastes good with their chilli too 😋👍🏼
Do not eat from this stall. The meat bak kut teh so hard and tough need steel teeth to bite off. Waste my money.
Okay! but just too hot to eat soup here. 3.6
One of the best bak khut teh is Singapore and is also recognized by Michelin. This is a must try when you visit china town in Singapore.
A different style Bak Kut Teh in Singapore. Yummy 😋 😋

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: The hokkien mee did not have overpowering wok hey, so the distinctive taste of hokkien mee shines through. Slurpy and tasty, spoon after spoon without getting too jelak.4th star goes to old school taste that it's hard to find nowadays.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: Fried on the spot! So good. 😊 The prawns 🍤 are so fresh cos the turn around is so fast. I always buy this when the queue is less than 5. Must pay by cash 💰. I have brought my friends from overseas and they all liked it. They put the chilli 🌶️ on the side and it’s not mixed in. Michelin bib gourmand 🌟

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
Added another Michelin hawker stall to my list.
The queue moved surprisingly fast despite the weekday lunch crowd—there were about 10 people ahead of me, but I only waited 15 minutes.
I was a little disappointed, though. The prawn flavour wasn’t as intense as I’d hoped; the noodles were quite wet and lacked noticeable wok hei or a strong prawn taste. That said, the $7 portion was very generous, with around 6 prawns.

The chilli wasn’t particularly impressive either.

All of this is just my personal preference—I’m not criticising the stall at all. Please go try it for yourself. I’ve simply had non-Michelin Hokkien mee that I enjoyed more.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
Honest plate for HKM. Ordered the $7 portion. Taste wise nothing to shout about, minimal wok hey. ingredients is fresh, sotong not chewy, prawn has a nice bite and sweetness, portion size is good.

Can eat if less than 10 pax in queue.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: tried the Hokkien mee after seeing the long queue. Despite the crowd, service was fast and I waited only about 10 minutes. The hawker and his daughter were friendly and efficient. The noodles had decent wok hei, though the flavour was a bit on the mild side and definitely needed chilli to lift it. Ingredients were fresh and well cooked. Overall, a solid and enjoyable plate, especially if you like a lighter taste profile.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
It's been many years since my last visit to this stall, before they first received the Michelin guide recognition in 2016.

There was a long queue, around 15-18 pax ahead of me during lunch time.  Luckily there was no one ordering many plates/packets, the queue cleared within 15-20 minutes.

When I saw the slice fish cake on display, I already quite disappointed.

I ordered the $7 portion and it came with five prawns (one prawn hidden below and only found it when I was half way eating).

Happy with the large serving portion and five medium size prawns.

Disappointed with the taste.  No HKM taste.  It is like an average normal fried noodles.  The chilli saved me.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
Noisy atmosphere because got singer

Dont expect too much from this Michelin guide fried hokkien mee

No wok hey
Queue for 5-10min
But when is your turn, took 30sec to get the food

Taste very so so, without chili will make it worse
Better request chilli, chili not spicy so dont worry

Worth to try but not worth to come back again

Good luck

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: 出汁が効いていて美味い

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
$6 plate. Taste good. But no wok hei. Portion was ok.

As a resident, but work in china for many years. I Usually skip stalls which only accept cash.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: I hold a great deal of respect for the two gentlemen operating the stall, but I found the fried sotong prawn mee to be somewhat underwhelming. If you reside in the vicinity, it might be an acceptable option. However, those who make a special trip to TB Market specifically for this dish might find themselves a little disappointed. I hope I just had a bad batch. I will try again and update this comment.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: Noodles lacked wok hei and tasted rather bland, and required the chilli to provide the flavours. Do note that there is no pork in the $5 plate. Otherwise, the amount of ingredients were rather generous. Cash only.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
Hokkien mee ($7 for large plate) - Came with 5 medium size prawns, sotong slices and fish cake slices. Good squid slices. Good strong prawn flavour in gravy.

From an earlier visit:
Everything was great except it’s just 4 small prawns for $5 plate. Otherwise great flavour and fresh ingredients.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: No frills fried sotong prawn mee that draws a queue. The line moves steadily as the chef cooks and serves up plate after plate of al dente yellow noodles and thick bee hoon, mixed with fresh prawns and slices of squid and fish cake. There are three sizes to choose from ($5, $6, $7) and the stall accepts cash payment only. The chili adds a layer of spice and umami to the dish that won’t numb your taste buds. Squeeze a splash of calamansi juice over the noodles for a zesty lift to this classic local noodle dish.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
超級好吃
Uncle一次會炒一大鍋
如果裝完了會在重新炒一鍋 所以會等比較久

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: Typically eat Hokkien mee only for dinner.., always see this stall with long queue, happen to be no queue., quickly buy and have it for early lunch…a really plate of Hokkien mee 👍🙂

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
I always miss Singapore’s fried prawn noodles. Whenever I come to Singapore, I will look for different stalls to try. This stall is quite famous in this area and always has long queues. I finally had the chance to eat here, but I was a bit disappointed—it’s not as good as the one I ate at in Yishun. Still, it’s not bad.
我一直想念新加坡的炒虾面。每当我来新加坡时，我都会寻找不同的摊位来尝试。这个摊位在这个地区很有名，而且总是排长队。我终于有机会在这里吃了，但我有点失望——它不如我在Yishun吃过的那家好吃。尽管如此，它还是不错。

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: Friendly service and good food. Very affordable.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
Many in Singapore and ashore has heard or read of Hong Heng. No surprised since they have been listed on Michelin since 2016.
I had multiple revisits way, even way before 2016, and they have been pretty good at their craft.
This visit in 2025, I noticed the noodles used now is dramatically shorten (cut), and more chewey than how I last recalled. The chilli paste was also different, some how.
I had the $6 plate, and it was laden with more seafood than most, and the flavour of umami and savoury still reminisce of the old. But somehow I felt I recall it was drier and packed more wok hey in the past. Maybe my goldfish memory escapes me...
It is still good, yes. But I am not so sure if it is my top 3 now, even though it has Michelin's blessing in 2023.
I must commend that service has improved, now that there is an extra guy taking orders, I don't see the wok shifu cum owner getting all so flustered and bothered.
Do go pop by and let me know how you feel?

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
海鮮出汁がよく聞いたホッケンミーがいただけるお店
ミシュラン獲得店
5-10分くらい並んだ
海鮮出汁がよく効いててとても美味しい
5,6,7ドルのオプションがあって、大きさを選んでいくかんじ。
現金のみでpaynowも使えないのが残念
ライムのトッピングはあるとより美味しい
端に載っているのは辛いソースなので辛いの苦手な人は避けたら良いと思う

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: Hot weather but good food

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
Hong Heng Fried Sotong Hokkien Mee @ Tiong Bahru food center.

Joined the long queue to try Hong Heng’s fried sotong hokkien mee, partly because it’s Michelin-recommended and seemed very popular.
Ordered the small portion. Maybe my expectations were too high, but unfortunately, the taste was quite ordinary and didn’t really hit the spot for me.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: Michelin star fried hokkien stall that attracts a large crowd during peak hours. My usual order is small version with added prawns & sotong. flavourful and tasty fried hokkien mee. Highly recommended.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
This one has that pork and prawn stock emulsified with noodle starch flavour. The amalgamation that some describe as “old school” Hokkien Mee.
Sambal is the cooked type too! Which is the way of old. Not the blended sambal belacan that some sellers have introduced out of convenience.
The only gripe I have is that the prawns they use, have a very pronounced “sand vein”, which can be seen in one of the videos. I understand that it is too much work for Hokkien Mee sellers to devein prawns but maybe a better source/supplier might help.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
Friday, 4 April 2025
Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee 鸿興炒蘇東蝦麵

Over-rated and no luck with this fried hokkien mee stall with so many Google rave reviews.

For $6 dine in serving, I got a plain plate of fried hokkien mee without wok hei and tasteless.

Plenty of leftovers (see photo). Sorry, but I just can't force myself to finish it.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: One of my favourite Hokkien mee.

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews: This modest plate of fried Hokkien mee is flavourful and delicious till the last bite! 😋

Restaurant Name: Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee
Reviews:
Joined the queue and ordered 2 big packet to share back home.
Don’t understand the hype, not very flavourful. Does have old school taste, prawns are fresh. Good thing is even I tabao home and microwave heat up, it’s not soggy and dry.
Don’t mind trying again, if there’s no queue.

Ordered cordyceps chicken soup for $5.50

Summary
Flavor : mild
Thisty? : no
Chicken : good
Cordyceps : great
Lychee : good
Soya Chili : Xiao la

Soup was mild. Not much herbal taste only sweetness. Freshing don't feel thirsty after drinking.

Chicken is somewhat off the bone. Lao le so don't expect it to be tender but is a soup so expected.

Cordyceps is like a supervisor of enoki. Well fungus after all.

Lychee gave the soup the sweetness, not sure how much sugar was added though.

Dip chicken into chili to get some small kick.
Nice soup, very homely and the lady boss is very super nice and kind. Love this!!

Oct 2025: Once again, they are awarded the Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2025! Soups are still as good

2022: As the name suggests, the soups here are very yummy indeed! Nourishing, healthy and delicious bowls of soups!
原本是應該給五星，可是排骨肉有部份口感很柴，帶骨頭的排骨才會比較嫩一些。令人訝異的是骨頭也很容易咬碎，可以吃下去，也就是說燉的夠久。湯頭很有冬瓜味。還不錯
This was a rather decent soup. I would be back to try their other soups.

Have been patronising the stall for #7 minced pork with mushroom, home cooked tasting, not overly salty or oily, generous with mushroom, most importantly the meat is really lean - does not have those fatty or scrape parts. Have tried the soups as well #4, 5, 8 but #7 is still my go to.

Ordered No 5 with rice for $6.
Chicken drumstick with fall apart meat in the soup, come with stringy chewy mushrooms & Logans. Overall not bad, however still feeling hungry even with rich.

Suggest to other something else and soup as a side dish.

No 1 is often sold out so curious to try that if have the chance.

Seen a lot of customers do take away and some bring their own container. This shows that they come with the intention to buy already. Queue can get long sometimes.

Just be patient withe the nice old lady
Really diluted and mediocre. Soup is more flavourful in their other branch.

12 Feb 2025: I returned this round to try more of their soups for lunch. We had the spareribs soup with winter melon ($4.50) and the night-blooming cereus spareribs soup ($4.50), and both were quite good. This was my first time trying night-blooming cereus, and it had an interesting texture—it’s smooth and slightly slimy, somewhat reminiscent of eggplant, though not exactly. Overall, it was pleasant.

15 Oct 2024: I visited around 6:30 PM for dinner, but most of the soups had already sold out. The only options left were two chicken soups—one with cordyceps flowers and the other with Brazilian mushrooms. I opted for the chicken soup with cordyceps ($5.50) and the pumpkin with minced meat ($4). Both were decent, but I’ll definitely come back to try them during lunch hours.
I always craved for the soups and meat patty with pumpkin here. Today I went late. The meat patty was sold out. Must visit soon.
Very good soup. Lady boss is a friendly HK lady. Opens 12 noon.

Ordered a winter melon soup with steamed pork ribs. Both are good. Double boiled soup is full of flavour and meat just right. Steamed pork ribs were done with black beans and not too salty. Overall it’s good value for soup and meat dishes.
Had steamed pork ribs with rice for dinner on 16/7/24, was good. I'll be back to try other items.
Every bowl of soup is a pleasure. I especially enjoy the one with various kinds of mushrooms. Probably one of the healthier option you could get in a hawker.

There is usually only 1 lady manning the stall, and she painstakingly scoops up bowls after bowls of soup individually upon order, ensuring fair amounts of ingredients going into every bowl

Hence, there may be a bit of a wait esp during peak hours.

But the quality of the soup...

OMG~! At the price point, I'd rank this as one of the best.

Soup was alright, chicken was bland but there was plenty of chewy cordiceps.
What was off-putting was the owner's attitude towards casheless payment.

There was clearly a QR code on the wall but the owner intentionally hid it away from view. When asked if I could pay with QR code, she chided how young people these days couldn't bring and pay with cash. She also insisted on looking at the amounts you keyed into your app and aggressively stated how if she did not receive your payment, she will make the customer pay twice again.

Please bring your patronage elsewhere no matter how decent the food is. You do not want to ruin your lunch with such an attitude and service.
No 1 and  8 is very good. And between the 2, 8 8s exceptional.

PayNow QR code scam!! Payment transaction completed and successful but stall lady insisted that she did not received it. End up paying cash and got to contact bank to void the transactions. At the time of writing this review, have not gotten any confirmation from bank if it is possible to revert.
She insisted and was adamant on the payment being on NETS instead of PAYNOW. Will never return due to the fraudulent nature of her business.
Extremely recommended.

pls do NOT use paynow or paylah. As many have shared, so many have fallen scam and victim to double payment as the lady will refuse to check her bank but instead demand you pay again in cash.

DO NOT GET CHEATED!!! @HongKongYummySoup PLEASE RETURN OUR MONEY!!!
Diluted soup

a cheating store that uses paynow as a front to demand more money from you! NATIONAL ENVIRONMENT AGENCY (NEA) pls LOOK INTO THIS!!!! woman will also blame you for "not listening to her" when the money has clearly gotten to her, but she will claim she did not receive.

paid money but did not get my food. The woman at the stall was really suspicious. When i asked about the possibility of paynow payment, she said ok. When i started to make the payment, i verified with her the name of the shop but the shop started rambling on about how it might not get through. I tried paying anyway, and it went through and i showed her the confirmation from the bank.

To my horror, she insisted that the money didnt get through and demanded that i pay her cash. The QR code clearly showed the name of her shop,  and the money did indeed go through and that was confirmed by the bank after i had to call in to verify. The woman was clearly LYING when she said she didnt receive the money.

i did not get my food but made the full payment for it. A very upsetting experience.

POTENTIAL SCAM ALERT: lady will tell you that paynow/PayLah can be used but when payment has gone through, she will insist that she did not receive the money although you have email receipts to confirm that payment has gone through. We ended up not wanting to pay double, as she demanded cash from us, even after we showed her proof that it has gone through. We ended up paying the full amount but walking away without our food because we refused to pay again in cash.

Had to call the bank to report fraudulent transaction and even so, bank can only try to retrieve the money through their “best efforts”.

Lady will insist that she has informed you to “test out 0.10” but that is a ploy to distract and confuse you. BE WARNED.

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews: Attracted by the stall’s Michelin award and strong Google reviews, we arrived with certain expectations for the beef 拉面 and 小笼包. The beef was good, and while the 拉面 was tasty, it didn’t quite feel freshly pulled on the spot. A small warning: the portion of noodles is huge — easily enough for two. The 小笼包 had a thicker skin, but the meat inside was flavourful. Overall, it didn’t fully meet Michelin‑level expectations, but it was still a good meal nevertheless. Price was affordable - total $10 for the 拉面 and 小笼包.

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews:
Ordered the beef lamian @$5

The good: portions are very generous, both noodles and beef slices.

The bad: soup is a little too bland. If u don't take chilli, its even more bland. Noodles are not handpulled, so lacking in texture.

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews: Tried Xiao long bao & guo tie (fried dumplings) and both were really cheap and the serving was generous! Each dish only costs $5 (for around 10 dumplings each)! Although the xiao long baos' filling were full of meat and has nice balance of of meat & veg but the skin was too thick imo. The guo tie (fried dumplings) were meh cause the batter was too hard and the filling were not that juicy.

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews:
Mixed mince and century egg porridge $4

Affordable and the male staff is friendly.
Will try dumplings next time.

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews: The dumpling is good. From the skin to the filings it is all handmade. 来试试就知。

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews:
Had pratonised this shop since day 1...
Quality of food is consistent n always good

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews: Absolutely loved the food! The La Mian noodles were perfectly chewy, and the Xiao Long Bao were juicy and full of flavor. Fresh authentic and delicious

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews:
チャイナタウン駅近くのホーカー。シンガポールで朝の定番のお粥を食べていなかったので来店。
時間的なのか、ローカル感が強いです。
種類がたくさんあるのですが、言葉が通じず、パネルで伝えて注文しました笑
量は多く、魚の切身？や野菜が入っていました。
思ったよりも味が濃く、美味しかったです。
優しいけど、しっかり食べられるので朝には良いかもしれません。
サトウキビジュースをこれに合わせて飲んでいる人が多くいて試しました。
朝にマクスウェルフードセンターでチキンライスを食べた後でしたが、食べれました。

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews:
Fried dumplings came freshly deep fried and hot.

Dumplings were of std size as anywhere else.

Meat fillings were mildly marinated which I like. I’m not in the habit of dunking them into the black vinegar sauce. But I do like the ginger shreds.

For $5/- I think there were like 12 dumplings. I was busy eating till I lost count. 🤭😅

I was shock at the portion when my beef noodle in soup arrive.

I am quite a big eater and I think tat bowl could share with another buddy.

Noodle was al dente mildly chewy texture which I like.

Clear Broth was flavorful but not overpowering. Till it makes u jerlak.

The star ingredient must be the chunks of slice beef. And also very generous.

Not really an expert on beef cuts. I think it’s along the tendon meat area of the cow. 😅

It was shoik for me to bite into them. Overall taste wise was well paired &  balance with the noodles and soup.

Not those heavy local beef noodle in soup laden with herbs and spices

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews:
I always get the chilli oil dumplings from here. $5 for 10 PCs I think.

I do not recommend the Xiao long bao. Broth is bland and sometimes it is not steamed well. They also break easily.

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews: Idk how people are giving this store 5 stars. The taste was mediocre, if not worse. Something smelt off about the XLB. By the time I came home I was completely nauseous and threw up the whole meal.

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews: The food was so good and so affordable :3 $5 for xlb, $5 for the fried dumplings (12 pieces) and $4 for this huge plate for chilli cucumber. The service was also very good, they were very kind :)

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews: Braved through the beer-drinking crowds for these plump and meaty morsels that is so worth checking out for its affordable price and legit native Chinese fare! The handmade xiao long bao with slightly thicker skin boasts an impossibly flavourful broth and juicy meat that we just can’t get enough of.

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews:
Amazing - most recommend the no. 17 Shandong dumplings (that can be also purchased frozen). The no 12 spicy dumplings are very good too ($5 - the ones with chilli flake, coriander, and green onion topping). Don’t forget chinkiang vinegar + a dash of soy to dip.
I’ve had better xiao long bao but they were fine.
Head two doors down to Shaxian snacks for a $4 large snow dry beer for the best pairing!

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews:
The Xiao long bao in this place is amazing! Ended up coming here every day during my stay.

Food courts in Asia are always a vibe!

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews: Very worth it prices. $4 for shredded chicken congee and it was all chicken leg meat (not breast meat), and it had lots of chicken. The guo tie is also worth it, $5 for like 10 pieces. XLB is okay, 6pieces for $5 soup is good, minced meat is also okay. Food wise not wow but all worth its price.

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews: Just spend ur money on McDonald's. U will be happier.

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews: Portion is huge and at a very cheap price. We paid $14 for all these, food is not bad, worth a try!!!

Restaurant Name: Hong Peng La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Reviews:
This is a visit across 2 visits, one week apart. First visit I had their flavour beef noodle and a week later their spicy shred chicken noodle. Hua Xing Bak Kut Teh: A Worthy Hunt for a Table, A Triumph for the Tastebuds!

My inaugural visit to Hua Xing Bak Kut Teh was a lesson in navigating the delightful chaos of a popular hawker stall. Let's be honest, the initial hurdle was securing a table during the peak lunch hour. For a first-timer, the "find a table first, order later" system required a bit of on-the-fly strategising, a mini-adventure amidst the bustling crowd. After a brief, strategic scan and a polite request to share, I finally secured a spot and dashed back to the stall.

The anticipation, however, was well worth the effort. My order consisted of their signature Bak Kut Teh, Pig Trotter, and Preserved Vegetables (Mei Cai), a trio of dishes that delivered on every level.

The Bak Kut Teh was a delicious and healthy enjoyment. Unlike some versions that may carry traces of fats around the pork ribs, Hua Xing pork ribs were firm on the bite and fat free. The ribs went well with the aromatic, peppery broth and resulted in a bowl of simple, unadulterated comfort.

The Pig Trotter was equally impressive. The skin was gloriously gelatinous, the meat tender and flavourful, and the braising sauce, a perfect balance of sweet and savoury, was utterly addictive. It was a dish that warranted my indulgence of a full bowl of white rice to go with the pig trotter and the accompanying savoury braised sauce.

The Preserved Vegetables (Mei Cai) provided a welcome counterpoint to the richness of the meat. The slightly sweet, earthy flavours of the mei cai, braised to a melting tenderness, were a perfect accompaniment, cutting through the richness and adding a layer of complexity to the meal.

Despite the initial table-hunting challenge, the food arrived surprisingly quickly, less than 30 minutes after ordering. And the value for money? Exceptional. Generous portions, quality ingredients, and flavours that exceeded expectations.

Hua Xing Bak Kut Teh is a testament to the enduring appeal of traditional Singaporean hawker cuisine. The bustling atmosphere, the efficient service, and, most importantly, the incredible food, make it a must-visit. I'm already planning my return, this time with a group, to fully enjoy the trio of dishes I sampled, and to explore their steamed fish, which I've heard rave reviews about.

I’ve been coming to Yuhua Village Food Market for a long time and have tried basically all the chicken rice stalls here. I don’t mind long queues — I queue early and I’m fine waiting. But I’ve had enough of this particular stall’s queue management, because queue cutters are repeatedly allowed, and even served first.

Today I joined the queue at the back (approx. 15 customers ahead). While waiting, I saw multiple people walk up from the opposite side (they were not in the queue) and order directly at the counter, and their orders were accepted and served first.

This isn’t about my turn being cut — it’s the pattern. I’ve seen queue cutters being accepted on other days too, and today just happened to be the last straw because it was so blatant: an uncle walked up from the side when it was my turn and the stall took his order and served him before me. Right before I left, another person walked up, scanned the QR code for payment (was expecting her to join the queue behind), ordered without joining the line and was also served first. When this keeps happening, it sends the message that cutting the queue is normal here. I understood should the customers had disabilities or were seniors with mobility issues but this is rarely the case at this stall.

It feels like the stall has become complacent because business is always strong and most people just want to get their food and move on, so nobody says anything. But that doesn’t make it okay. Long queues are fine — unfair queues aren’t. I won’t be returning unless the stall enforces a single queue and serves only the next person in line.

For anyone deciding where to go: the Hainan Chicken Rice stall on the other side is just as fast, the food is good, and from what I’ve seen they actually ask people to queue properly. If the queues are too long, there’s also a soy sauce chicken rice stall behind in the same market, or the chicken rice stall at the coffeeshop behind (normal rice).

Always a fan of Japanese food, I asked my friend to find something new & exciting!

So, before we start:
DONT GO IF YOU DONT LIKE NOISE!

In a restaurant that is primarily counter seating (there are 2 private rooms & 1 tea room) one needs to be conscientious of other diners! Oh well, I guess $$$ don’t buy class!

The Chef: Ms Akane Eno, is not new in town, apparently at present location 5 years, prior 2 years at Robinson Quay , she was gentle but also appeared a bit stressed!

The Classical Japanese counter, partially wood, also stone, classical layout, not bad, serves its purpose!

The Menu, check their website or go through reservation, and for lunch you have two choices, Akebono at 138,-$ or Shinonome at 188,-$, plus when you are seated you are given a choice to upgrade from Beef to Unagi for additional 22,-$ as well as an additional Handroll at 22,-$ as well!

It was a special celebration so we opted for the works! Plus a half bottle of Bubbles! Devaux, which was surprisingly pleasant!

The Food:

Starting off with the classic Sashimi Box, a tad too warm for my taste, quality was good though, well cut, the shell ark was good, marinated fish excellent, the egg a classic

7 out of 10

Next up was the Shawanmushi with King crab meat and Japanese eggplant! Great consistency, flavour good!
8 out of 10

The Extra, the Ankimo Handroll, a classic, tasty, and well made in front of you!
8 out of 10

Following was chef’s signature dish the Somen , Ebi, Uni, Timburi & prawn stock, it was served cold, Uni great prawn a bit overcooked, else decent
7 out of 10

A sort of main course, was the Tuna Cheek Miso Yuan. Which I personally felt was the best dish of the day! Super tender, extremely well cooked, together with the Matsutake Mushroom, a real winner!
9 out of 10

The Tai Ohba Fry, was a sea bream in seaweed crust, decent but for me a tad too dry?
6 out of 10

Another Highlight was the Donabe Rice, we opted for the Unagi, which was really excellent! Great consistency & flavour
9 out of 10

Dessert was nice, Houjicha Ice Cream plus some fresh fruit!
8 out of 10

Overall a pleasant meal, service was good, although quite busy with that group!

Chef is good, I would probably like to try again if I knew the restaurant was a tad more quiet!

Chef Akane-san has elevated my Omakase experience to a new level. I chose this restaurant to celebrate my special milestone and it was so worth it with a tailored crab themed menu. Every dish she presented was a blown-away savoury journey. What made it even better is the sake wine, winter sake wine she recommended to pair with the menu. Outstanding!

If you want to experience a fine dining experience that awakens all your senses, and wows your partner(s), Akane-san (the Master Chef) and her restaurant is highly recommended. We totally enjoyed the yummy food, attention to the smallest details. Looking forward to going back soon

Absolutely fantastic.  Our lunch was better than any fine dining meal I’ve had in Tokyo.  The flavors and presentation of each dish was phenomenal. Everything tasted so clean and fresh it’s amazing that everything is imported from Japan.    I strongly recommend!

I treated myself to a birthday lunch at Ichigo Ichie and left with an unforgettable culinary experience. From the moment I mentioned my dietary restrictions, the chef thoughtfully curated a menu tailored to me, making me feel truly seen.

The sashimi was fresh, but the smoked scallops stole the show with their deep, rich flavors, perfectly setting the tone for the meal. An optional add-on of handrolled ankimo was a decision I’ll forever cherish—creamy, decadent monkfish pâté at its finest. The chef’s signature somen was another standout. Delicate, chewy noodles in a light broth with prawns, bafun uni, and a spicy miso dollop created a medley of flavors that was pure bliss. The lightly sautéed abalone with abalone liver sauce paired with a crispy Japanese puffed rice cracker was an elevated delight. The unagi rice bowl was exceptional, and transforming it into ochazuke with the flavorful broth made it feel like an entirely new dish.

The experience was seamless, from top-notch service to personalized touches like a beautifully crafted linen napkin gifted by the chef. Every dish felt like a note in a harmonious orchestra, and I cannot wait to return for another special occasion.
Good quality sashimi, enjoyable lunch with fresh ingredients. This hidden jem at a corner of Claymore Connect is worth a visit.

It was our first time to try a Japanese restaurant with female chef and the matsutake oakase. The decoration of the restaurant is simple, generous and comfortable. The chef is gentle, careful and intelligent with exquisite skills, which can well reflect the quality and deliciousness of the ingredients.

At the price we paid for lunch, the minimal expected standard is enjoyment. Thankfully the restaurant delivered over and beyond. Won't ruin the surprise for others so just posting a few photos. The food was premium, complex, and hearty.
Love the chef, food and service! We will be back!!

Its our first time here and we thoroughly enjoyed our dinner at Ichigo Ichie. Food was delicious, we tried 2 different sake, both were great. Not the most "atas" omakase restaurant, but I totally love the "homely" vibes the restaurant gives, and the sincerity of the Chef. We are already planning to be back in the near future.

I can't say enough how much we love Chef Akane-san's cooking. She's so creative. And she's always spot on with her wine/sake pairing. We just went to a special sake pairing dinner featuring sakes from Yukawa sake brewery (16th generation!) and we were blown away about how much of a magician Chef Akane-san was with the dishes. The ingredient combinations were very unusual and the dishes really made the sakes taste even more special.

Amid the tough competition among quality choice Omakase and Kaiseki restaurants, Ichigo Ichie caught my attention because of the unique menu and the head chef, Akane Eno, who is the only Japanese female chef based in Singapore. In fact, I had experienced Chef Akane Eno’s cooking when she was still in Kimura many years ago. I remember that she was very meticulous and assured when preparing the dishes for my lunch. So I’m all eager to suss out how things go with her helming the restaurant.

Yes, I’m totally wowed over by every dish of this Kaiseki dinner. There is a good reason why this restaurant has lots of regulars. Palates are constantly surprised by chef’s innovative creations.

I can feel this quiet sincerity when savouring the food prepared in various ways. The food is rustic yet delicate and fine, traditional yet unique and novel. There is a subtle boldness in incorporating new curated ingredients (Hibiscus Jelly, anyone?) to make the food taste more exciting and refreshing.

The restaurant’s setting is of minimalist Zen, with pine wood counter and clean, simples, classy surfaces. A stone counter behind the kitchen counter adds that rustic homeliness to the place.

Service is very thoughtful, professional and sincere. I really enjoy my time here.

Chef's Signature of Miwa Somen with Kuruma Ebi, Uni and Tonburi is so full of goodies and different essences of the sea. The briny prawn stock coats the smooth cold somen to slurpy goodness. Creamy umami from the uni plus firm, briny sweet, succulent prawn make this dish more luxurious and multifaceted in both texture and taste. The tiny dab of surprise, yuzu chili, makes this more exciting.

Tairagai, a rarity in Japanese restaurants here, spellbinds my palates at first bite with its unique smoky, briny flavours and springy texture akin to scallop but firmer. An important component of this dish is the Hibiscus Tea Jelly, which is refreshing, slightly tangy and adding a gelatinous texture to the dish.

Awabi Croquette is the best croquette I ever have. Abalone is cut into tiny pieces and added into the mild milky, savoury custard to introduce bits of this awesome crunchy texture. This is simply brilliant. Abalone Liver Sauce has this earthy umami to enhance the taste. Green Asparagus from Japan is fresh and crunchy.

Kegani Dumpling Soup is clear, light and briny sweet. This is pure comfort food. Japanese Hairy Crab packed into the thin smooth dumpling skin is full of sweet essence of the ocean.

Ayu Japanese Sweet Fish is surprise of the day where its bitter, sweet flavour develops to intense savoury goodness with Sansho Ankake. Yamato Toki imbues the fish with herbal flavour to make the taste amazing.

Japanese Wagyu Beef A5 Miyazaki Sirloin is creamy, oily meaty, sweetness manifested, tempered with charcoal-grilled meat smokiness. Organic Cacao gives hint of bitterness while tomato adds a refreshing element for a complex, pleasing, memorable taste.

Donabe Rice is packed with Unagi, Taiwanese Dong Ding Oolong Tea and crunchy, juicy, super sweet Japanese White Corn. It hits all the sweet spots on both taste and texture. Savouring this reminds me of the fragrant rice fields.

Genmaicha Ice Cream is uniquely toasty and sweet, made even better with the saltiness of Shoyu Jelly and floral tangy sweetness of Mango.

Thoughts: Rustic Yet Delicate, Subtle Yet Bold, Incredibly Unique Experience
お酒の種類が多いのであかねさんにリクエストしていただきました。美味しい sake を選んでくださって、ありがとうございます。シンガポールはどこも日本食は高いので、お値段はさておき、丁寧なお食事とサービスでした。お料理は純日本食というより、少しシンガポール人向け食材なのかな？と感じました。

Finally make it to chef Akane new location restaurant at Claymore Connect . She took over the defunct restaurant Kappo Kaji location . I have been her regular for every season menu . Her cuisines is not for everyone as it tends to be on the lighter side rather than heavy . New location new ideas and new direction which I like it better than from her last location . It seems that the menu price has been raised but I am not complaining as the ingredients used are of the premier type . They are still running in the service and the FOH need to do more work to improve . They have a new tea pairing which I highly recommended. I will return for sure to see how she has progress further .

A real gem and extremely underrated, Chef Akane and team always exercises finesse in putting together super well-balanced flavours and textures of Japanese cuisine that REALLY HIT THE SPOT using really high quality ingredients.

There are only a handful of restaurants in town which make me want to go back and taste their dishes again during the different seasons to experience the chef's unique creations, and Ichigo Ichie is one of them.

There's always a couple of standout dishes each evening that make every diner at the counter have an expression change with their eyes closed for a few moments to process how good the dish was 😂

It's also really interesting to try the different produce chef sources from local farms, craft beer / sake / umeshu that chef personally and passionately selects or creates herself!
my favourite japanese fine dinning!!!
Lovely experience
My sister's favourite restaurant. Very lovely private experience. We enjoyed the warm nature of the chef and the array of food which was served to us. Will definitely come back.

インターコンチネンタルホテル　2階にある和食懐石のお店になります。

女性の方が料理人で
前菜からデザートまで産地、調理方法、調味料などこだわり丁寧な仕事が素敵なお店です。

The food here delivered by Chef Jake Lee & Team is at an exceptional level, worthy of 2 Michelin stars at least and looked visually stunning in photos too! There was a lot of finesse and passion that you could see on display from the team at the open kitchen. Came here for the first time for a Valentine’s Day celebration with my wife and we were delighted by every course with spot on flavor balance and perfect interplay of textures. Some misses that marred an otherwise outstanding meal:

1) Table assignment which was confirmed 15 days ago was not fulfilled and I had to show my WhatsApp conversation with the team to reconfirm, was initially seated just beside kitchen.

2) There was no table crumbing service and I had to request for it after a few courses were served and the table was untidy. Last photo as example. This is a basic professional service standard let alone at a Michelin establishment.

3) I was presented final bill for payment and since I was asked to pay a deposit beforehand to reserve table, I wanted to confirm deposit was going to be deducted from the full amount since there was no record of deposit on the bill but both staff who handled my bill told me the full amount was correct and they had no idea about the deposit and I had to show them my PayNow (see last screenshot) and WhatsApp message as confirmation that I paid the deposit. This process is unusual. I was told later by another staff to trust the process as they would’ve deducted the deposit when I made payment. Most places would give you a final amount less deposit before they proceed with payment.

Clearly the kitchen & menu is managed at the highest level as for the rest of the operations there is hope that one day they can reach for the 2nd star. I wish them all the best.

Some dishes were great while others are not- this is pretty subjective based on personal taste. Writing this to share more on the service. Similar to what others pointed out, tables are very close and every conversation could be heard clearly. There was a huge ant which climbed into my bread and butter, told the staff and she just took it away… no apologies. No service recovery. Heard the next table being asked their preferred doneness for the beef (main course), I wasn’t asked. I took my own initiative to check with the staff and she said the default is medium rare and asked if I was ok, I said no and shared my preference. It came medium rare (first photo) and I told her could I have it the way I requested. She said it’s medium well. I showed her it’s not. She reluctantly took it, and it came back still medium rare (second photo). If it’s not a true choice, perhaps don’t even ask? I know some places are strict so make it upfront if it cannot be done any way else? after this sending steak back incident (I really really didn’t want to but I don’t like medium rare) I noticed everyone shunned my table as if im some troublemaker. I didn’t make a big fuss and spoke nicely. overall not a good experience.

Really cosy and smooth experience. Food was delicious and I loved the cold inaniwa dish with the amazing wine-like tomato.

I don’t take alcohol so wished they had a more extensive drinks menu to cater to that.

Special mention to the hot and crispy ginger madeleines that made the menu feel more festive. The other table also gave their compliments to the chef for it.
Just perfect

Food 8/10
Service 11/10

Had a fine meal at Iggy's.  Had some stumbles at the start but finished strong

The snacks/amuse bouche looked exciting but was a major letdown.

Bafun uni on yam. The uni looked so fresh but was immediately was overpowered by the yam. The combination did not work at all. What a waste! I should have eaten the uni separately.

The tuna tartare on hash brown was so so. The hash brown was very oily.

The last was a cold pumpkin soup with tofu. That was excellent.

Inaniwa udon that followed was  good - smooth , silky enhanced by the tomato consomme. Very fresh and light dish.  But It came with shreds of snow crab which was dry and hard causing disharmony to the overall taste.

Carabino salad was good in its parts but didn't come together. Felt like one piece of prawn with a greens on the side.

Things got better from here,
The foie gras was buttery and smooth

The cappelini was a beautiful fusion of japanese umami and italian finesse. Loved every bite

The tennen buri was gorgeous.  The applewood gave it a smokey richness that complemented the buttery and fresh sweetness of the fish

The tenderloin was good but nothing exceptional. A good piece of meat cooked right.

Dessert was good and so was the madelines. I always remember them having a great pastry chef

Service was spectacular. I walked in without prior reservation and requested some mix and match to the menu and they did their best to accommodate with a smile.  Service was attentive. Kudos to the team!

I had lunch at Iggy’s recently. It felt like seeing a good friend I hadn’t met in a long time. Not much has changed in terms of aesthetics but that is more than made up for on the plate. Iggy’s menu consists of familiar fare, dishes which are simultaneously delicious and comforting. It doesn’t try to be overly uncomplicated but it is no less delectable. Each dish is a testament to the freshness and quality of the ingredients, the skills and techniques of the chefs and their ability to showcase this without the eye watering price that sometimes accompany these kinds of meals. Speaking of accompaniment, the Pouilly fumé and Savigny-les-Beaune by the glass make for a wonderful pairing!

Amazing experience start to finish. Service was impeccable and completely unintrusive - it never felt like they were anxiously hovering around, yet they're immediately there when you need them. Perfect. Food was also top notch - one of the few Michelin places that I actually felt was deserving of its star and status. Not a single bad dish on the lunch tasting menu. The fish was a revelation - exactly what a good fish steak should taste like. Full of natural flavour. Best thing was that the staff also wasn't pushy about beverages - a true testament to good hospitality. Will definitely return.

We decided to celebrate our Silver Wedding Anniversary once again at a Michelin-starred restaurant, this time in Singapore, so we chose Iggy’s, located in Voco Orchard, and delighted ourselves with the food. We were fascinated by the creativity, subtlety, and delicacy of each dish.

With great versatility in its offerings, which bring together a fusion of contemporary cuisine, we enjoyed everything from the flavorful Snow Crab with Tomato Consommé to a Duck Confit, masterfully prepared and served over a bed of white asparagus. The next dish was one of the best Gnocchi I have ever had, with a Mushroom Ragout and Arugula Pesto, crowned with a crispy slice of Ham—simply finger-licking good.

For the main course, we chose the Manganji Pepper, perfectly balanced with shavings of truffle that melted in the mouth.

After the delicious dessert, we were pleasantly surprised with a refined gesture: a special dessert prepared to celebrate our anniversary, beautifully decorated and truly touching.

An unforgettable evening.
Congratulations to Iggy’s—we wish you much success and many more Michelin stars.

Wanted to try solo fine dining and chose Iggy’s following a friend’s recommendation. The restaurant was very attentive and called me multiple times to confirm I am indeed going just by myself (yes! Pls normalise eating alone!). Service was top notch, they really try to make you feel at home.

Food-wise I thought they could be more attentive to temperature. The finger food appetiser served on top of a frozen lime - I was told to bite into the lime for a better flavour but it’s really difficult to do that when it’s literally ice-cold and ice-hard. Then the next appetiser had a cod fritter which was scalding hot!! Almost burnt my tongue.

Mains were great, I loved the longtooth grouper. Dessert wise, it might be worth thinking of having two desserts variant to match the two main options. The wagyu was quite greasy already, to have a caramel-based palette cleanser then a milky dessert on top of it just doesn’t make sense. Perhaps something acidic to balance it out? Just my two cents.

Mini madeleines are awesome, thanks for letting me have a second round.
The meat is very plain
Iggy’s is an excellent place to come to enjoy a wonderful dinner or lunch. Love it! And Iggy is a wonderful person.

VOCO 3Fにあるが、検索にまだHiltonが出るため日本人は場所を間違える事があるとか。今回家族で利用し温かいサービスと最高の料理を堪能できた。snacksから楽しめ、シンガポールの要素も散りばめられたどこかホッとできるヒュージョン。料理のテンポや声がけもこちらの表情や流れを見てスマートなサービスだった。

I last visited Iggy’s years ago when it was still in a hidden corner of the Regent Hotel, when it was one of a mere handful of ambitious new eateries at the leading edge of what was to become Singapore’s contemporary fine-dining movement. Back then it was exciting, innovative, and remarkably unstuffy with its counter seating and close contact with the chefs.

At Voco, the interior design is still defined by a sleek, low-key sensibility (the main entrance is so well hidden, it looks like a side door); the chefs are now safely corralled behind a large glass window, and so the FOH now takes on the role of social contact, which they do well. Despite the fact that Iggy’s nowadays has to jostle elbows in an ever-burgeoning gastronomic food scene, the food has remained engaging and true to Iggy’s east-west DNA.

The “Gastronomic” degustation menu is well-executed and beautifully plated, and consistently plays between the twin poles of French and Japanese cuisine. Pumpkin tofu, a Hokkaido scallop carpaccio, a salad of red Carabinero prawn, and a jap-influenced karasumi linguine were all delightful.

The stars, for me, were the 2 main courses: a longtooth grouper, and the Bresse pigeon. The longtooth, a firm white Japanese version of the familiar fish, was paired with duck confit and a duck-infused bourguignon sauce (!) which turned out to be an inspired combination. The pigeon, pink and tender, was exemplary. Iggy’s has a long tradition of playful pop culture-inspired desserts; the Rocky Road, a high-end interpretation of familiar carnival fare, went down well, as did its “corny” palate-cleansing predecessor.

The service was ever able, knowledgeable and warm. Much recommended.

Iggy's, Singapore: A Fusion of Global Flavors and Refined Gastronomy
Iggy's, a long-standing one-Michelin-starred restaurant located within voco Orchard Singapore, is a true institution in the city's fine dining scene. Under the visionary guidance of restaurateur and sommelier Ignatius Chan, Iggy's has carved out a unique niche by offering "Modern European cuisine with Asian overtones," primarily focusing on exceptional seasonal produce from Japan and around the world.

Ambiance and Atmosphere
Iggy's provides an elegant and intimate dining experience. While it may not boast panoramic skyline views, its refined interior creates a cozy and sophisticated atmosphere perfect for quiet conversations and special celebrations. A key feature is the picture window offering a glimpse into the kitchen, allowing diners to witness the culinary team in action. The meticulous decor and comfortable seating contribute to a tranquil environment, ensuring guests can fully immerse themselves in the gastronomic journey. For those seeking even more privacy, private dining rooms are available.

Culinary Philosophy and Highlights
Iggy's is renowned for its seasonal, ever-evolving tasting menus, reflecting the dynamism of the international culinary scene adapted to the Singaporean palate. Chef Ignatius Chan, with his deep knowledge of global ingredients, continuously pushes culinary boundaries. The cuisine is characterized by modern European techniques infused with subtle Asian flavors, often leveraging premium Japanese produce.

While specific dishes may change, some themes and popular creations that have graced Iggy's menus include:

Premium Sliders: Often featuring decadent ingredients like Kagoshima Wagyu with Epoisse cheese and brioche buns, showcasing a miniature yet sophisticated take on comfort food.

Sakura Ebi Capellini: A timeless classic, this dish features al dente pasta coated in umami-rich lobster oil, topped with crispy Sakura ebi, kombu, and sorrel, highlighting a delicate balance of textures and intense flavors.

Wagyu Beef Creations: Dishes featuring high-grade Wagyu (like Miyazaki Wagyu) are expertly prepared, often paired with nuanced accompaniments that complement the richness of the meat.

Seasonal Seafood: Given the focus on fresh produce, expect exquisite seafood preparations, such as Hokkaido Scallops with Oscietra Caviar or innovative fish dishes.

Deconstructed Desserts: Iggy's often presents unique and artful desserts that play with textures and unexpected flavor combinations.

The menu also caters to diverse preferences with vegetarian and plant-based gastronomic menus available, demonstrating versatility and a commitment to high-quality ingredients for all diners.

Wine Program and Service
A defining feature of Iggy's is its extraordinary wine program, curated by Ignatius Chan himself, a celebrated sommelier. The restaurant boasts an extensive cellar of over 25,000 bottles, with a particular emphasis on rare and exceptional Burgundy wines. This impressive collection allows for impeccable pairings that elevate the dining experience.

Service at Iggy's is consistently described as impeccable, personal, and highly attentive. The staff are knowledgeable about both the food and the extensive wine list, providing seamless and unobtrusive service that anticipates diners' needs. This commitment to warm hospitality ensures guests feel valued and comfortable throughout their meal.

In conclusion, Iggy's offers a refined and memorable culinary adventure. It's a destination for those who appreciate high-quality ingredients, innovative yet harmonious flavor combinations, a world-class wine selection, and impeccable service in an elegant and intimate setting.

Lunch at Iggy’s at Voco Orchard Hotel was a treat for the senses—each dish in the $150++ tasting menu was beautifully plated and layered with sophisticated flavors. There’s always some crispy, sweet or savoury elements tantalising your taste buds.
The golden eye snapper with inaniwa udon and apple snow was a bright, zesty opener, while my favourite was the foie gras paired with white asparagus and duck confit - rich and decadent.
The gnocchi with mushroom ragu and jamon crisps was earthy and comforting, and the tenderloin with truffle jus was melt-in-your-mouth tender.
Dessert—a yoghurt creation with black sesame and osmanthus—was a refreshing finish.

Service was impeccable: our waitress was attentive, friendly, and even offered to help us with photos, adding a personable touch to the cozy, intimate ambiance. Coffee was available as an add-on at $10 per cup—pricey, but in line with the overall indulgence. Overall, a classy spot for a special occasion, though your wallet may need a moment to recover after the bill.

My first visit to Iggy's was a truly notable experience. As a solo diner, I appreciate establishments that offer a comfortable and welcoming atmosphere, and Iggy's certainly did.

The food was a highlight of the afternoon. Each dish showcased a thoughtful approach to cuisine, presenting flavors that were both pleasant and engaging. The creations were interesting and held my attention throughout the meal.

The staff at Iggy's were notably friendly and attentive. They ensured my needs were met without being overly intrusive, contributing positively to the overall dining experience.

I found the service pace to be just right. Unlike some other establishments where the meal can feel prolonged, Iggy's maintained a steady flow. Courses were served efficiently, allowing for appreciation of each dish without any sense of rush or undue delay.

Iggy's maintains a high standard, and I would recommend it for anyone seeking a refined dining experience in Singapore, whether dining alone or with others. I look forward to returning.

Dining at Iggy’s at voco Orchard Singapore was a beautifully paced journey through refined flavors and seasonal Japanese ingredients with European finesse. The evening started with delicate snacks like shiro ebi and pumpkin tofu, easing into standout courses such as the Tennen Buri with caviar and shiso oil, and a silky Murasaki Uni dish featuring Hokkaido scallop and inaniwa udon. The King Crab with Japanese rice and crab miso was deeply comforting, while the Poulet de Bresse offered a classic yet elevated touch. The cheekily named Iggy’s Happy Meal — featuring Miyazaki wagyu, epoisse cheese, and amela tomato — was playful and indulgent. Dessert, a thoughtful blend of Dekopon orange, black sesame, osmanthus, and yoghurt, was light, floral, and the perfect ending. Elegant, restrained, and masterfully executed — Iggy’s remains one of Singapore’s finest.

Last week was my birthday, so I did what any sensible adult would do — made a plan with my friends to justify spending way too much on fancy food (because once a year, we deserve it, right?). This year’s pick: Iggy’s at Voco Orchard Hotel.

I chose it mainly because their lunch set sounded relatively reasonable at $150++ — keyword: sounded. I added the wine pairing for $115 because, you know, birthday logic. The lunch came with five courses, all very polished and Western-style, with top-notch ingredients.

Was the food good? Yes. Was I full? Not really. Was the bill a little soul-crushing? Absolutely. I was mentally prepared for indulgence, but when the final amount came, I still gasped a little inside.

But hey — if the produce is premium and it’s just a once-a-year splurge, I’d say it was a classy way to celebrate (with a side of mild financial panic).

The meal was unremarkable. While the appetizers were excellent, the main course, a fish dish, was mediocre.  Although we typically anticipate the dessert with enthusiasm, it failed to meet expectations, necessitating a visit to the hotel cafe for a more satisfying conclusion to the meal.  However, the service and ambiance were exceptional.

A good experience dining at Iggy’s. Food is designed creatively; having ingredients not commonly seen together such as uni with butter, inaniwa with apple. Tenderloin is perfectly cooked. Sake ice cream is one of the best.

Delicious food and fantastic service by the staff. They are attentive yet not intrusive, with a warm manner. This is so difficult to find in Singapore. Highly recommend this restaurant — oldie but goodie. Food still manages to wow.

恰逢一位经常与我和好友一起吃饭的朋友生日，于是订了久违的米其林。

这家算老牌米其林，这几年一直在榜上。午餐价格适中，五道菜150（不含税费），坐落在Voco酒店三层，门口并不显眼，推开门别有洞天，暗黑色装修，隔成大大小小的房间。我们这个房间很有意思，有一个很大的玻璃窗，午餐开始时，卷帘升起，后面是干净明亮的厨房，可以看到每一道菜的诞生，宛若大幕开启，演员开始舞台剧的表演，等最后的甜品上桌，卷帘放下，宣告表演结束。

从餐前小食就能感觉到这家米其林是法式和日式的结合，我最喜欢金枪鱼塔塔，同事喜欢带柠檬酱的炸小球，后面的前菜更是彰显日本风味，开胃的乌冬凉面配一种叫金目鲷的鱼，紫苏青酱的米型意面配萤火鱿鱼，丝瓜海带汤配马粪海胆。整体都是清新路线。主菜我点了牛里脊，同事点了鱼，牛里脊很嫩，但上面的黑松露一般味道很淡并没有起到画龙点睛的作用。

同事的生日，这里贴心的上了一小碗乌冬作为长寿面，甜点上还点了蜡烛，让人感觉很好。甜点的冰激凌口味很特别。

lggy‘s的服务很好，保持着一种发自内心的关注与热忱，且每一位服务生都保持着同样的水准，注意观察食客的状态，在合适的时机提供服务，使食客倍感舒适。

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Iggy’s on February 21st, where we were treated to a private room experience for five guests, hosted by the gracious Susanne. From start to finish, the evening was a celebration of exquisite culinary art.

Upon arrival, the service was impeccable. The staff provided a thorough introduction to each course, detailing the inspiration and ingredients behind the dishes, which created an engaging and thoughtful atmosphere. The attentiveness of the service team, especially Susanne stood out—every need was promptly addressed, and dietary requirements were accommodated effortlessly, with dish changes made swiftly and without hesitation.

The meal itself was a stunning seven-course tasting menu, showcasing modern Japanese fusion at its finest. Each course was meticulously crafted, presenting a perfect balance of flavors and textures. The ingredients were fresh and vibrant, and the presentation was as visually stunning as it was delicious. From delicate sashimi to perfectly seared meats and innovative flavor combinations, every dish delighted the senses.

The fusion of traditional Japanese elements with modern twists was a true highlight, pushing the boundaries of what one might expect from a fine dining experience.

In conclusion, Iggy’s provided an unforgettable dining experience, where exceptional service and outstanding food combined to create a perfect evening. I highly recommend this modern Japanese fusion restaurant for those seeking a memorable and refined culinary journey.

Food: they are generally good but lacks the creativity for both taste and presentation. Nothing was bad but nothing was a wow either. The beef was sinewy. Forgot to take the picture of the beef.

Service: I have certain expectations of service in a restaurant like this. Granted that it was full house for Valentine’s Day but being short handed is not a good reason. Overheard the same comments from the couple next to us. 3.5 hours for the dinner with long wait in between dishes. We had 3.5hrs long dinners before but not due to the long wait time between dishes. They might want to stagger or cut down on availability if the kitchen cannot handle it. I thought the kitchen wasn’t very efficient as certain dishes can definitely be prepared for more tables at the same time. However, this is coming for me who has no kitchen experience. Cutleries were presented incorrectly once. Another server had to replace the silvers with a wooden spoon that was placed by another server.

Finished with the kueh salat which was nicely layered and not overly sweet.

We visited on Christmas Eve with our family of five adults and two children. The restaurant was only about 40% occupied, yet we were seated directly beneath the air-conditioning vents. The children were freezing, and when we asked for coverings, we were told the only two shawls available were already in use. A request to change tables was also declined. The lack of flexibility and care was disappointing, and the evening quickly became uncomfortable, with the children having to take turns waiting outside with accompanying adults. Only when stern words were exchanged did the service staff take notice.

The food was largely stews, typical of Peranakan cuisine, but served lukewarm. Most dishes lacked freshness and seemed reheated rather than prepared with attention. There was little effort to brighten the flavours with spices or garnishes. One dish-chap chye arrived with raw pea pods tossed in, which only highlighted the complete lack of care.

The clientele appeared to be mainly mainland Chinese guests, with the occasional local tycoon. Service, however, felt perfunctory and indifferent unless one fit into those categories. For others, the experience was superficial and careless. Honestly, even food court service chai Peng was warmer by all accounts.

Overall, it was an unfortunate way to spend Christmas Eve, and I would not recommend this establishment.

Had dinner tonight at INDOCAFÉ and had a really nice, quiet evening. This was my fourth time here and honestly, I still love the black and white bungalow, it has such a nice atmosphere, elegant and iconic. Feels like a good place to slow down and enjoy a proper meal.

Over my visits, I’ve tried quite a few dishes, the Wagyu Beef Rendang, Nyonya Otah Otah, Ayam Buah Keluak, Vegetarian Fried Rice, Dry Laksa, and the Sago Gula Melaka. Overall, the food has been consistently good. It leans more towards familiar, comforting flavours rather than trying to surprise you.

I usually order the Wagyu Beef Rendang. It’s rich, flavourful, and very tender. Sometimes there are bits with more connective tissue, which gives it that slightly chewy texture, not really my personal favourite texture but the flavour itself is still great and you can tell the ingredients are of good quality. The Sambal Belacan is very authentic, and definitely not shy with the heat. Dessert was actually one of the highlights for me. The Sago Gula Melaka came with durian, and the durian tasted fresh and clearly well chosen. It worked really nicely with the gula melaka not overpowering the flavour at all.

Service was friendly and welcoming. They even gave us a complimentary dessert for a birthday, which was a nice touch. A couple of my reservation notes were not fully followed up on, but overall the staff were attentive. We arrived at 6pm and although they were busy with a large group, they still checked in on us throughout the meal.

All in all, INDOCAFÉ is a solid choice for comforting food in a beautiful, timeless setting.

Our group of 5 went on a Thursday afternoon for lunch.  After making a reservation we were informed the cancellation policy is $100 per person though we were not penalised when someone had to drop out (2days before) due to unforeseen event.  They were able to accommodate a last minute addition from 4 to 5 persons.

Wait staff were helpful in answering our questions and making recommendations.  We ordered ala carte so everyone can taste a bigger variety of food.

Belinjo crackers and achar were served foc while we waited for our food.
I was surprised to see they served otah ($16) with coconut cream (a block cut into 5 strips, coconut cream in a separate jar) but the taste was good.
Quintessential nyonyah dish ayam buah keluak ($29) was not bad; the buah keluak was stuffed with paste (not cooked whole) and was not too salty like some places do, but I didn't like the texture. A friend took the other two though, so they must be ok lah.

The wagyu beef rendang ($38) came in a serving of 4 chunky pieces but they were so very tender and tasty everyone gave their approval.

Babi pongteh ($28) is a sliced pork dish with mushroom and potato.  The sliced pork were very tender too, but I thought the potato i ate tasted a bit weirdly sour but no one else said anything. A friend said he liked this dish though for me it was quite forgettable (but I'm not a foodie).

Kari kepala ikan whole($58) is red snapper fish head curry with okra and brinjal. A foodie friend said this was a very generous serving of the whole head (usually elsewhere is half) with lots of meat.  Tasting it immediately bring to mind the curry that comes with roti prata but it was not that sour. It was mild enough for me to drink (I don't take very spicy food) though my friend thought it lacked punch (like Indian curry).

We shared 3 bowls of their jasmine-brown rice mix ($3.80), yet didn't finish (not that the portion was big) 😑 & were too full for dessert.

We were asked if we wanted sparkling or still water, though someone in the group noted they have jugs around (they actually serve water but never offered?) The waiter opened a 3rd bottle of San Benedetto still water ($7.80) without our asking, and they waived the charge upon our protest.

The restaurant was not too noisy; the ladies like the ambience. I noticed they have private rooms.  Parking was free but as a fellow-diner said, max 5. We went up the front stairs into the restaurant so I don't know about wheel-chair accessibility.

I was really impressed with this Peranakan restaurant. The food tastes truly authentic, and you can feel the thought and care put into the seasoning of every dish. The service was also warm and attentive. I especially appreciated the thoughtful touch for the Ayam Buah Keluak—they provided wet towels and proper tools, which made the dining experience even more enjoyable.
