I'm back at Omakase@Stevens for another season! Actually, there are some really awesome restaurants that I always want to go back, if I have the time, and for Omakase@Stevens, this place is one of the exceptional restaurants that I make time to come here every season. Every visit here is full of delightful, rare surprises that showcase the flavours of each season. And this time, a meal here feels like a beautiful trip through Japan during Autumn.

The flavours and looks featured in this menu speaks of the mellow autumn with earthy tones of red and brown. What is amazing is that while the mellow tones are primarily featured in the dishes, they are all very unique and different from each other in the taste profile, making this an exciting journey. Every dish is a standout on its own.

Jose and his team are such wonderful hosts. Their service is absolutely top notch.

First of the Hassun Trio is minced Maguro perching on top of Rice Cracker and topped with Caviar and Oyster Flower. This is like the sweetest blue fin tuna I had ever tried. It has three different layers of briny sweetness stacked on top of the rice cracker with an hint of mild nutty taste.

I’m so excited, for the first time, to try Gougère, a kind of choux pastry whose dough is mixed with cheese, Nire Cheese in this case. I totally love it. The pastry looks simple at first glance, but the taste is like the beautiful intricate pattern of the cracker on top: complex and intriguing. The core of the gougère is bursting with this nutty sweetness of cheese, tempered with the savoury, earthy depth of miso.

Wagyu Egg is like a signature dish at this restaurant because of this deep intense warm sweetness of different kinds that immediately wows over my senses at first mouthful. To make it even more amazing is that some ingredients will change between seasons to ensure a surprise every time. This time, crunchy juicy peanuts are added for the earthy sweetness, complementing the beef’s savoury sweetness and the light whipped cream’s milky sweetness. It’s magical.

Goose Liver soaked in Shitake Mushroom consommé and topped with Chrysanthemum is the best Foie gras. The juicy, bouncy foie gras has the texture tending more towards that of gelatin than paste, and I absolutely love it. The clear earthy sweetness of mushroom perfectly balances the heavy taste of foie gras to yield the taste of earthy unami.

Ikura and Hokkaido pumpkin balls meticulously laid on top of smooth Egg Custard looks so beautiful. And the taste is just as beautiful. It is definitely the most briny sweet chawamushi with the most multifaceted texture. And the taste actually gets better with subsequent bites.

Amadai, which is Tilefish, tastes absolutely amazing when paired with Yuzu Kosho and Daiginjo sauce. The specially deep fried crispy skin highlights the incredibly succulent juicy texture and light sweetness of amadai.

The Beef, which is from Kagoshima this time, is prepared into Cutlet form so that the super fine, crispy deep fried exterior highlights the super juiciness of the beef. The beef is so unbelievably juicy and meaty that.

Sigature Donabe is so briny sweet and tastes surprisingly earthy with Japanese Oysters added. The rice tastes so starchy, smooth, completed with a good bite. It is so satisfying and such a joy to savour this.

Waguri dessert is really like that signature dessert of Autumn, with the earthy goodness of Japanese Chestnut, tempered with bitterness of Hojicha and the light airiness of Wasanbon. Usually, chestnut tastes earthy and usually very grounded. So it really surprises me by being earthy  and yet heavenly airy light at the same time.

Budou dessert features a grape feast of Shine Muscat, Red Muscat and Kyoho injected with a blend spices like cinnamon. This is like three different desserts on one plate.

Thoughts: At here, I just realised that Autumn is such a lovely season!

I picked this spot to catch up with an old friend—partly because they just got their first Michelin star, and I was curious to see what the buzz was about.

The restaurant is located on the ground floor of a separate building next to the Novotel on Stevens Road.
To be honest, the location isn’t ideal.
You might be able to get there by MRT or bus, but there aren’t any obvious landmarks around, so we just took a taxi.
The entrance is very plain and doesn’t give much away. But once you step inside, it shifts into a calm, well-crafted Japanese space.

The restaurant is compact, with counter seating wrapped around an open kitchen.
It was fully booked when we went.
Two Japanese chefs worked with their assistants to serve each course with great pacing—no long gaps, no awkward waits. The staff were observant and well-timed with drinks and dishes.
They were friendly, but didn’t overstep or chit-chat unnecessarily.
I liked the balance. The space is brightly lit, which personally I really appreciated.

The food was beautifully presented, using seasonal ingredients flown in from Japan. The variety of cooking methods and plating made the whole experience visually fun and well-thought-out.
That said, not every flavour worked for me—but that’s more personal taste than anything else.

One small note: there are two entrances, and if you walk in through the middle one, you basically arrive right in front of the counter where people are already seated and eating. It’s not a huge issue, just something that caught my attention.

All in all, it was a calm, well-executed experience with thoughtful dishes and smooth service. I’m glad I chose it for a quiet reunion.

🍄 Spanish Omelette – loaded with local mushrooms & drizzled with mushroom XO butter — earthy, buttery goodness.
🍝 Creamy Mushroom Mafaldine Pasta – luxurious, creamy, packed with umami. Pecorino = perfect tangy finish.
🍗 Smoked Whole Sakura Chicken – juicy & aromatic, thyme jus, crispy skin, chilli relish on the side, served with fluffy Niigata rice.
🥞 Buttermilk Pancake – soft, golden, topped with banana brûlée & BBQ banana ice cream (yes, BBQ!) with soy sauce meringue twist.
☕ Deconstructed Tiramisu – layers of Kahlua sponge, mascarpone foam & coffee jelly — light but indulgent.
🍋 Lemon Meringue Pavlova – zesty key-lime mousse, caramelised lemon ice cream, and milk chips? Chef’s kiss.
🥥 Drinks – Kaya Toast Latte (iced) = creamy, toasty, nostalgic. Also a solid hot cappuccino to round things off.

The garden-to-table concept is refreshing and genuinely inspiring 🌱. Food’s delish, plating’s beautiful — perfect for brunch dates, fam outings, or chill catch-ups.

Expect lots of pets, kids, and good vibes all around 🐶👨‍👩‍👧‍👦💫

I haven't been here in a long time, but this place remains as lovely as ever, situated near the Botanic Gardens. It’s a little sanctuary if you’re not fond of the busy Dempsey Hill area. The female staff were very kind and attentive; she kept coming back to refill our drinks. The bartender, especially when serving the drinks, took the time to explain what each one was. We had a meal for four, and we ended up sharing most of it among the four of us.

We recently held our wedding at Open Farm Community, and it was truly one of the best decisions we made. Our guests were delighted with both the food and the service. The focaccia bread, mains, and fruit juices (especially the ginger beer and mango mint) received countless compliments.

We were very worried about mosquitos because of our experience during rehearsal, but the team lit mosquito coils and the problem was reduced with the help of simple mosquito repellants. Many guests shared that the celebration felt like a warm gathering and thoroughly enjoyed themselves.

A special mention goes to Chris and Nino, who were incredibly responsive to our queries and ensured the venue was well-maintained and fully stocked so that our guests had the best experience possible.

If you’re looking to host a cozy and intimate wedding, we highly recommend reaching out to the team at Open Farm Community!

We arrived just before 2:30 pm, only to be told the kitchen had already closed and no food was available. It was disappointing to be turned away when it was still within normal lunchtime hours. Avoid if you’d like to be guaranteed service during opening hours.

Back again for the oysters, bread and veggie tempura — still so good. The ambiance and service are wonderful, and dining here feels like being transported somewhere away from Singapore. A perfect spot for fresh oysters, bites and a relaxing escape.
文字通り、農園の中にあるレストランと言えるでしょう。食材へのこだわりが感じられるお料理でした。

Loved the fact that they have their own garden and grew their own ingredients. Food was honestly average for me and the highlight of everything was actually the starter bread they provided. Bread was amazing and the spread, was out of this world!

Been wanting to try this place for a while and finally did, it did not disappoint. The Wagyu beef burger was one of the best we’ve had, the pulled pork eggs Benedict was rich and satisfying, and the burrata? An explosion of flavours in every bite. The space is bright, airy, and has a feel-good vibe that made the whole experience even better. Will be back!

Ordinary almost fast food like at super inflated price. Service is okay. But not worth it. The concept about “farm to table” is nice, but I don’t see how beer battered fish and chips at $36 or a Wagyu burger is in line with this concept. Coffee is terrible. Seriously feel like not much thought given into food & drink.  Just an honest review, that this place is super low on value, taste. Need to do better

Haven't had such a bad meal for ages, it's truly awful!
First off, the waiter was just weird, he gave the feeling that he was working at a hawker center and accidentally transferred to the restaurant. Then came the starters which was okay, except that the crackers that came with one of the dishes were soggy.The mains - I ordered medium rare steak, half of the steak came well=done and the other half rare, so on average it was medium I suppose. The coffee mash potato just tasted off, imagine eatting instant coffee with instant mash and rubbery meat, the whole thing was just disgusting.
The food was really fresh and delicious. I ordered Hokkaido scallops, pork chop and oysters! Every dish was really up to the standard. However, I feel that the price is on the higher side.

Tucked in a quiet corner of Dempsey. Love the rustic atmosphere
Burger               8/10  very good fries
Avo Benedict    8/10
Food was mediocre. Don’t have too high hopes.

I don’t know how but they got avocado toast wrong - no flavor and somehow didn’t taste like fresh avocado.

They were unable to make dietary accommodations (for example, my friends didn’t eat eggs and they were not able to substitute the egg in the avocado toast for anything else except additional avocado). While they were pleasant and service was overall good, they food was below average (especially for the prices) and we won’t be returning.
Wonderful service and exceptional food.
Food amazing. Servers on top of it.

Wow… the food… was just… AMAZING!
I gotta say, the night started off frustrating. It was day after valentines and we had a reservation for 8:45pm. We showed up 10 minutes early and weren’t seated until 9:25. Nobody came to update us until I checked in with the staff myself, but after we finally sat down and got our orders in it was about 9:45. So we are 1 hour into our dinner at this point and expectations were LOW… but it turned around quick.

Our waitress was awesome! 👏🏽 she recommended fantastic options for us and also explained the menu super well. We ordered two pasta dishes and one entree to share.

We had all 3 dishes come out at the same time and wow… wow wow wow… incredible. I am not one to boast about food but WOW 🤯 ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS. The duck was braised so beautifully and was the most succulent duck I have ever tasted. It was flavor PACKED inside and out with the most delicious crispy skin. Both of our pasta dishes were incredible. Flavors were BOLD and every bite had us wanting more. At no point did we ever experience flavor fatigue. Every bite was unique and we were able to mix and match flavors that all blended so well together. Thank you Osteria Mozza for one of the most delicious meals we have ever experienced. Chefs kiss 🤌🏽 price seemed a bit high but for the first time I would say the food justified the price. Well done chef, absolutely stunning creations. Wishing blessings on the business!
Compliments from Portland Oregon!
the agnolotti is sooooo good

The food 100% lives up to the restaurant's reputation. Delicious across the board.

Service was almost perfect.

During peak dinner hours, it's too loud to have a conversation without raising one's voice.

I made a reservation for Osteria Mozza ahead of time, but we still waited about 30 minutes after arriving, which was frustrating. Inside, the restaurant looks classy and elegant, and the atmosphere feels special. The waiters were very nice, attentive, and professional throughout the night. The raviolo and other pastas were outstanding and easily the highlight of the meal, while the steak was good but not amazing. One small surprise: our waiter saw lots of butter on our plate and offered a piece of bread. We said yes, assuming it was complimentary, but they brought a large half loaf and charged us $8. Overall, the food tastes great and the experience is pleasant, yet the prices just didn’t feel worth it for what you get.
testy

Excellent experience - not surprising for a Nancy Silverton restaurant! Vibe on point. Food amazing. Servers on top of it. Food highlights were the Burricotta & Spiced Walnuts (the sweetness with the light spice on the walnuts = perfection) and the Butternut Squash Tortelloni. And don’t skip on the garlic bread (hot tip if it gets sent out first: save it to go with your pasta). Zero misses though foodwise - was all amazing. The balsamic on the steak gave it amazing flavor. The salanova was nice and light with such good flavor - loved the crunch of the fried chickpeas.

Dinner at Osteria Mozza was indulgent, comforting, and unmistakably Italian in spirit - the kind of meal that leans into simplicity done very, very well.

We started with the octopus, perfectly tender and well balanced, followed by a spread of burrata & prosciutto and fresh mozzarella that reminded us why Mozza built its reputation around dairy - creamy, delicate, and absolutely worth the hype.

For mains, the pastas were the real stars. The ravioli was rich without being heavy, while the tagliatelle delivered that deeply satisfying, silky texture that only well-made fresh pasta can achieve. Nothing overworked, nothing overstyled - just confident, honest cooking.

Dessert didn’t disappoint either. The tiramisu was classic and comforting, and the chocolate mousse was smooth, indulgent, and perfectly portioned to end the meal without excess.

We paid around $160 per person, which feels justified for the quality of ingredients, execution, and overall experience. Osteria Mozza doesn’t chase trends - it focuses on doing the fundamentals exceptionally well, and that’s exactly why it works.

Great food, service and atmosphere ! Exceeded our expectations. Highly recommended.
An incredible experience,food is excellent

We had a large party with a set menu and truly wonderful food and generous portions. The branzino was unexpectedly one of the best dishes I’ve had in a long time.

The service was warm and kind, especially from the bussers, runners, and server assistants.

What really rubbed me the wrong way was having our server literally roll her eyes at us for handing her multiple cards at the end of the meal. We could not have been easier guests and modern POS systems make this very easy. Not to mention the hundreds of dollars in tips. Seemed very stupid and unprofessional at an otherwise nice place.

I’m a huge fan of Chef’s Table and I love fine dining, so I visited this place during my California trip. I had heard it was an Italian restaurant, so at first I didn’t expect much and only ordered a glass of Prosecco. But as I tried each dish, I was blown away .
I immediately decided to order a bottle of wine 😂🤣.

I went with the dishes recommended by our server, and they were absolutely amazing. The wine we chose with the sommelier’s guidance was perfect too. The space was beautiful, and if I lived nearby, I would definitely come back again very soon 💕.
Great atmosphere, fresh high quality ingredients. But superrr expensive and there nothing I would say "I am craving it or must have it again"

I'm sad to say, Osteria Mozza was such a disappointment, after having watched Chef's Table and all the awards this place has (James Beard, 1-star Michelin), I was let down by the entire experience. I've been to numerous bib gourmands, 1-star, 2-star restaurants and this might be the worst of all the Michelin recommended spots I've been to. The service was slow and the food was slow to arrive as well. We got a variety of appetizers/salads/pastas, and everything was completely plain and lacking in any exceptional flavor or "wow". Several of our dishes we left unfinished. This place felt very run of the mill Italian, but with the high Michelin prices (5 plates totaled over $200). Definitely skip this one unless generic Italian at high-prices is your thing.
First time at Osteria Mozza! Service was incredible, food was great, and the vibes were great! I even got a handwritten Happy Birthday note from the team. Very cool experience
Delicious! Quite expensive and small portion but I guess food is just overpriced in LA these days sadly.

Comer pasta nunca decepciona, pero en un restaurante con este renombre, estrella Michelin y un precio elevado, siempre uno espera más.
Es divertido comer en la barra y la carta de mozzarellas es muy variada, pero el sabor no de acerca a los platos y pastas de nivel de otros restaurantes (o de cualquier local de Italia).

The food was okay for the price and quantity, desserts were delicious and they have a nice wine selection with a very welcoming sommelier. Host was pretentious. The duck confit was a healthy quantity and five stars.

Went for a work dinner with 5 colleagues. I liked the round tables so we could see each and engage but the restaurant is incredibly noisy and busy so I really couldn’t hear anyone across the table. The menu is interesting and everything is a slightly different take on Italian favourites. Food was a bit mixed in my opinion, somethings were amazing and some were average. Service wasn’t very attentive and I felt like we were often ignored, we would have ordered more food and drinks but getting a waiter was too hard. Also my clothes smelled terrible of burnt oil when I left and I’m travelling so it meant I couldn’t wear any of those items again on my trip.
3 if 4 meals sub par. Probably should have went to Burger King.

Just had a dinner with my wife at this restaurant. Beautifully decorated giving the authentic Italian restaurant feel! Service by the staff was excellent and attentive! Plates were changed after every course. The burrata with crispy garlic, chilli, anchovy tasted very unique! The iberico pork is so tender with the fat layer simply melts on your mouth! Wrapped up with the fantastic dessert nicely decorated! Recommended!

On Tuesday 3rd, March, the family went to Osseria Moza at the Hilton Singapore was my daughter's first choice for her birthday dinner — and it's easy to see why she loves this place. What makes it so special isn't just the food, but the extraordinary level of care and hospitality that the team brings to every table.

From the moment we arrived, the service was warm, attentive, and genuinely made us feel looked after. It's the kind of hospitality that turns a nice dinner into a truly memorable occasion.

A very special mention goes to Angelo, a senior waiter who was the perfect host from start to finish. He had that rare gift of anticipating exactly what you need without ever feeling intrusive — professional, charming, and genuinely warm. He made my daughter feel like the guest of honour she absolutely was. He didn't just serve us; he looked after us.

Angelo and the whole team — thank you for making her birthday so special. The service alone makes this a place we will always come back to.

Im posting this review in appreciation of Raj! He is definitely a gem staff. His hospitality is top notch with sincerity and warmth. He knows what he is doing and does it so well. Becoz of him I ordered a wine and a serve of the meatballs. The gigli pasta was good. I will come back here perhaps for the pizza but mostly, for the exceptional service from Raj

Food was lovely - traditional dishes were well made and experimental dishes were exciting, environment was lively and service felt intentional from Winsom despite a busy Friday. Will definitely be planning a trip back to try other things on the menu.

Osteria Mozza offers a refined Italian dining experience with a lively yet elegant atmosphere. The mozzarella bar is a highlight, featuring fresh, high-quality cheeses. Pastas are well-executed and flavorful. Service is attentive and professional. Prices are on the higher side, but the quality and ambience make it worthwhile.

Osteria Mozza offers an upscale Italian dining experience with a lively yet refined atmosphere. The mozzarella bar is a standout, and the pastas are rich and well-balanced. Service is attentive and polished. It’s on the pricier side, but quality ingredients and ambience make it ideal for special dinners.

Had the pasta tasting menu and opted for the wine pairing, which complemented each course beautifully and elevated the overall experience.

We started with a light ravioli where the cheesy flavour really came through. The second course was the amatriciana. It was delicious, though the guanciale was slightly chewier than I would have preferred. The lasagna that followed more than made up for it, especially with its crispy top layer that added a wonderful textural contrast. The final pasta was a fennel sausage cavatelli, flavourful and satisfying, even though I was already quite full by then.

Dessert was a delightful posset to end the meal on a bright and refreshing note. Thoroughly enjoyed the entire experience. A truly delicious way to carbo-load.

Went for the Amex platinum deal, overall a good experience.

Burrata was great, spice level just nice. Pastas and meat dishes were nice. The desserts were perfect for my partner and I, he really enjoyed the quality coffee gelato and I liked the heavy sweetness of the butterscotch (had to steal some of his waffle tho).

Was seated outside, so do know it can be very humid even with fans blowing.
Food was genuinely exceptional. Service very nice. Beautiful ambience.
Food was excellent. The olive oil rosemary cake was our favourite. Service was excellent too. We were celebrating a birthday, and the staff gave us a free scoop of ice cream and a hand-signed card
We had dinner here recently and it was wonderful. Everything we ordered was delicious, and even had some unique twists, and the ambiance was perfect.

Came here for the table for two from AMEX, happy with the quality of food and service. However between each dish, the wait time could be rather long as it's very busy

Appetizer was the best for me especially the fusion with the chili flakes. The beef cheek pasta was little strong tasting for my wife, but luckily I was ok with it. Iberico pork is good too, having some nice char at the sides of it.

Deserts was however too sweet for me but it might just be me

Great food, great atmosphere. Service was warm and friendly too. The pizza and the grilled meats are the highlights here!

Only feedback is that food could be a tad salty. Will ask for a little less salt next time.
Great service by Winson, and amazing food served in dimly lit alfresco dining. Ambience was lovely, would definitely come back again.
Amazing pasta, service was brilliant especially by Winson, will be back:)

Very nice italian restaurant. Went for the amex dine for 2 meal for lunch. They didn't have vegetarian options in the set menu but they gave us several options to make our meal and experience amazing. Arvind Raj was there to serve us and suggest many good options. The food quality and quantity and taste were all very good. Service was in the top I have had. It's not clear but they are in the hilton hotel and the hotel also has parking. You can also get a parking voucher if you have a meal here. What else can you ask for.

We booked our Amex Love dining dinner for two at Osteria Mozza.

The seating in the outside garden area was windy and pleasant. Menu had good variety and we enjoyed the cheese appetisers, pasta and mains. Portion sizes were just enough. However, butterscotch budino for dessert was too sweet and we couldn’t finish it.

Service was great, especially our server Aarvin Raj was joyful and efficient.

Recommend it.
Margie had incredible service recovery, was super attentive and showed high EQ. Thoroughly appreciate her service and hope she gets a raise.

We had the 4 course set meal. The food quality was good, however I find the serving between the course was quite long. In total, it took us about 2 hours from the time we arrived till we finished our meal.
Great food, and service was amazing - highly recommend the mozza bar and Iberico pork

Enjoyed my time here! The food was amazing and the atmosphere is just perfect—really cool vibe for a night out.
What really stood out, though, was the service. Everyone was so attentive and friendly, which honestly made the meal even better. It’s rare to find a spot that gets the food, the mood, and the hospitality all right at the same time :)
Lovely ambience with great food and presentation. Everything tasted amazing.

Was just here today for a birthday celebration. Table for 4. Food was great , however 2 of the mains did not arrive despite 3 reminders.
The pizza finally arrived and we waited another 15 mins for the last remaining main which was the pasta . On the 4th reminder then they realised that they forgotten to put in the order for the pasta. (sigh)

doesnt help that the pasta was meant for my 8 year old, so the poor fellow was starving and nibbling on our mains while waiting for quite a while..

Not a great experience. Food was very good , service polite and friendly but just disappointing overall as a dining experience which was a pity.
I love the pizza here, exactly the style I adore.  And the staff are awesome, always warm and helpful.
Everything was prepared with care.

Overall, the food is good. I particularly like their pork chop as well as the new dish which I believe is called ghili (is a prawn dish with bread crumb). For starters, we always go for mozzarella though we added their grilled octopus which was lovely in taste, esp the taste of grill.

The service is still impeccable. We have good exchange with both the sommelier and our waiter. I cant remember but my compliments to him for being attentive and also hospitable - a bespectacled tall, not bad looking guy with good English and able to converse in Mandarin too.

We were seated at the garden area which is lovely. A little warm for me but I believe would be comfortable for most, esp ladies. Able to hold a decent conversation too (and I am a little hard of hearing. 🤣)

Oh yes, I had my Hilton card so a decent discount too. :)

I still can’t get over the Banana Gelato Pie. It’s so rich, indulgent, and absolutely perfect for banana lovers. Every bite is incredible, and I keep thinking about it long after leaving. The handmade tagliatelle with slow-cooked beef cheek ragu was also really good—flavorful, tender, and comforting. The atmosphere is dim, cozy, and perfect for both family gatherings and intimate meals. The service is impeccable, friendly, attentive, and makes you feel genuinely welcome.

A whole wok will be fried up & serving those non-chilli plates systematically followed by chilli plates. Very fast frying and service.

They do, however, have an “excellent” business mindset: the moment you join the queue, staff immediately approach you to take your order and collect payment. The logic is simple — once the money is paid, you die die have to wait for your food.

Restaurant Name: Outram Park Fried Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: Very popular with loyal following of char kway teow lovers. Very fragrant and well cooked with pork lard. Can add extra serving of eggs and cockles with extra charge. Reviews: This is by far my favourite char kway teow. So flavourful and fragrant. Wok hei too. Must add chili to enhance the taste. Super long queue all the time, so be prepared to queue.

Restaurant Name: Outram Park Fried Kway Teow Mee
Reviews: I've been here multiple times. It is definitely one of the most famous hawker stalls in Hong Lim and probably Singapore. Their fried char kway teow has this wok hey, freshness of the lala, and noodles that are moist from the dark sauce. It is fried by an old uncle while his son takes the orders. They open around 11am and sell out by 2pm on weekdays, so do come early as the queue can get quite long. As the queue can take around 30 to 40mins, sometimes I would order a large plate of kway teow for the long wait.

Personally, I consider it one of the top tier char kway teow stalls - a must-try at least once !

Restaurant Name: Outram Park Fried Kway Teow Mee
Reviews:
…made it to Hong Lim earlier just before 7am and even then there was already a reassuring queue.

The cockles were of the non-hepatitis roulette variety,with none of those lurid,blood haemorrhaging theatrics that turn breakfast into a medical gamble.

The kway teow was springy and utterly unsoggy.Their shape held with quiet confidence.

The egg beaten into an almost carbonara state which lacquered onto the egg noodles and those thin delicate and faintly puffy fishcake slices.

Then there is the unmistakable wok hei…that charred,smoky perfume lingering dome-like over the plate announcing itself before the first bite.A scent potent enough to awaken even the most unsophisticated of olfactory systems.

What a morning gastronomic reprieve after a bicycle ride.

recently had the pleasure of dining at Pangium Peranakan, and it was truly an exceptional experience. The restaurant offers authentic Peranakan cuisine that is rich in flavor, beautifully presented, and clearly prepared with great attention to detail.
Every dish we ordered was delicious and packed with traditional spices and ingredients that highlight the uniqueness of Peranakan cooking. The flavors were well-balanced and comforting, making each bite memorable. You can really taste the authenticity and quality of the food.
The ambience of the restaurant was warm and welcoming, creating a pleasant dining atmosphere that made the whole experience even more enjoyable. The staff were also friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable about the dishes, which added to the overall positive experience.

21st of February 2026

Our family birthday dinner at Pangium was beyond just a gastronomic journey. It was the perfect blend of traditional Straits cuisine principles and creative culinary imaginations, conveyed through an innovative concoction of contemporary techniques and beautifully layered flavours.

One of our guests was of Peranakan heritage and she thoroughly enjoyed all the courses provided. Our experience was further enhanced by detailed, meaningful and even bilingual explanations that accompanied every course.

We want to express our most sincere gratitude to the kitchen and service staff for their homely hospitality and warm demeanour that elevated our exquisite and memorable experience.

We highly recommend Pangium for an evening of fellowship, dinner and even making friends with their enthusiastic kitchen and service crew.

Our huge compliments to Chef Lim, Jean, Rainer, Cha Yee, Ya Xin, Sherrine, Huat, Jazzaca, Nelson, Leroy and Joanne. Thank you for making our dinner a truly unforgettable one!

Having heard so many positive comments on Pangium, I finally made the reservation for lunch. Their menu is a reflection of their ongoing exploration of heritage Straits cuisine. It is an eye-opening experience to join this ever-evolving journey through the rich culinary traditions of the Malay Archipelago.

Chef Malcolm Lee successfully preserves heritage. On top of that, he adapts new influences into his cuisine creating his own hybrid cuisines.

All desserts are very delicious. I like sagun and musk melon sago in particular. It is highly recommended that you add Tau Yu Bak which is the best main dish among all.

I researched a number of places for fine dining for my wife and I's anniversary trip to Singapore. Nestled within the serene and lush surroundings of the Singapore Botanic Gardens, Pangium offers a unique and deeply personal exploration of Straits cuisine. Awarded one Michelin star, Chef-Owner Malcolm Lee’s second restaurant is a love letter to his heritage, presenting classic Peranakan flavors with a refined and modern touch.

The tasting-menu-only experience is a narrative, where each course tells a story of a long-lost or overlooked recipe. Named after the pangium tree that produces the iconic buah keluak seed, the restaurant’s cuisine pays homage to this heritage ingredient, featuring it in innovative ways—a testament to the chef's creative vision. The dishes are a harmonious blend of tradition and innovation, meticulously crafted to showcase the depth of flavor inherent in the cuisine's Malay, Indonesian, and Chinese influences.

The dining space is as beautiful as the food, with large windows overlooking the gardens that create a sense of tranquility and connection to nature. The service is attentive, professional, and knowledgeable, with staff often sharing the origin stories behind each dish. Pangium is not just a meal; it is a cultural and emotional journey that elevates heritage cuisine to a fine-dining art form, making it an essential stop for anyone seeking a truly meaningful culinary experience.

植物園深處，美麗的Pangium
因為這次沒有帶小孩，我們出發前就決定要去摘顆星⭐️室友研究了一下新加坡的米其林餐廳，最後選擇了這家取材當地食材，特色為馬六甲「海峽菜」風格，2024新進獲得米其林一星的娘惹菜餐廳。

首先要強調的是，它地點比較偏僻，在新加坡植物園一角的山丘上，建議各位不要！不要！不要！妄想要搭捷運來這裡⋯⋯⋯
因為我就被某人詐騙，跟我說走過去沒有很遠⋯⋯⋯結果我足足的走了半個小時，我真的快熱死！！

我從捷運出來後中間經過了森林、車道，看到一堆野雞跟被遛的狗狗，最後在一個兒童遊樂場旁，見到一個通往山丘上的階梯。
我：「你現在是不是要帶我去糖果屋？裡面會有巫婆拿著好吃的甜點給我吃，然後把我抓去賣掉？？？？？？」
室友：「我怎麼捨得呢🫣」
好不容易走進餐廳，餐廳人員聽到我們是走路來的，全部都露出非常震驚的笑容🤪🤪.... 連當地人都說遠，那就是真的遠 🤡

正確的交通指引，是使用新加坡的叫車軟體grab，它會把你送到最近的botanical garden gallop extension的入口，甚至直達餐廳門口。餐廳前身是個會展中心，旁邊是前法國大使館，是殖民時期建造，新加坡歷史最悠久的兩間「黑白屋」，所以如果在太陽下山前抵達，剛好能在用餐前多拍些美照！（但請千萬小心不要玩破褲子🫠🫠🫠🫠）

回到食物，所謂海峽菜，指的是凸顯馬六甲海峽的多元飲食與殖民歷史，融合各民族食材去設計的菜單。主廚刻意選用了許多當地的食材或食譜，例如店名的Pangium 就是一種原產於爪哇群島的果實，其種子經發酵後就成為招牌菜 Rawon Mee Sua （麵線）& Oxtail Satay （牛尾沙嗲）醬汁的原料，更特別的是侍酒師搭配上極甘口的山廢生原酒，壓制了醬汁的鹹味，互相映襯出食材的鮮味。

另一個特色是主廚堅持大量的手工流程，例如本日菜單上的Nasi Ulam & Buah Paya Masak Titek是一種將多種食材細切，搭配醬汁食用的香米飯，如果用機器研磨可能會因溫度的改變致使風味不同，所以主廚寧可慢慢切慢慢磨。眼尖的粉絲可能會注意到，主廚食指上甚至有個包紮傷口🤣🤣

這裡的每一道菜都會讓你有一種似曾相識的感覺，不是分子料理，但很多地方可以看出主廚的基本功跟創意。例如前菜的Pig's Brain Gado Gado，顧名思義用的是「豬腦」，服務我們的領班說這是前幾週剛開發出來的菜，主廚哄騙他說是豆腐腦，還真的吃不出一點腥味，只覺得很Creamy有乳酪製品的口感，搞清楚細節之後不得不稱讚主廚真是十分大膽！

Pangium製作的每一道甜點，也是結合了當地的飲食風味去製作，讓身為甜點胃的我超級滿足～例如第一道上的Sagun是一種新加坡傳統小吃，將椰子等食材反覆研磨翻炒後成為一種像糖粉一樣的東西，裝在芭蕉葉後倒入嘴巴吃，因為麻煩又賣不了多少錢所以現在街頭上幾乎看不到，在這裡則搭配雪酪食用，解膩的同時也讓人可以吃出椰子粉的甜味。真的是從前菜到甜點都讓人滿意的一家店！

整家店的服務也是很值得稱許的部分，非常有活力而且細膩貼心。當日主廚非常地熱情，沒有因為獲得米其林一星就自滿，中間會出來詢問顧客有沒有什麼需要改進的。你可以感受到這裡的員工是真心熱愛這家店，而不是照本宣科的社畜，像晚餐後由於已經11點多，當日主廚跟經理知道我們是外國人這邊不好叫車，還開著高爾夫球車送我們去植物園門口叫Grab 😂

我跟室友都很看好這家店的潛力，我們也期待這位主廚能再更上一層樓。

需要提醒的是，這家店定位為fine dining，因此沒有a la catre可以單點，只有兩種價位的套餐，兩種價格的餐酒pairing，原則上同行的人要點相同的組合，且不接待12歲以下的小孩。它的午晚餐menu 也不相同，只有週末中午有開放午餐，而晚餐的價位遠遠不只米其林網站上標示的兩顆錢幣....帳單一下子就讓我感受到室友的求生意志！雖然價格不菲，但下次造訪新加坡時，我們絕對會為了這次美好的體驗考慮再訪Pangium !

Overhyped, overpriced, and frankly dishonest team members.

First of all, calling this place “Michelin” is absurd. Tiny dots of food on a plate at outrageous prices? We paid $20–25 for THREE cutlet like patties or something, each the size of an Oreo biscuit: that is daylight robbery.

Fine, let’s say Michelin means small portions and an “elevated experience.” Then where is the elevation? Where is the innovation? There is absolutely nothing innovative here. This is basic South Indian food you get in India served on fancy plates and marketed as something revolutionary.

The idiyappam was okay at best. I’ve had far better idiyappam at roadside stalls. They tried to distract us with a gimmicky podi idli made with “pineapple podi” and a game of “guess the fruit to get a free dessert.”South Indians are rice eaters, (never even mentioned they are “ONLY” but it’s absurd to not have any in the menu except one biryani. The other in a combo. Charging $43 for biryani and curry when the taste is just “good” (not extraordinary) is unacceptable.

Ambience. People act like this place is visually groundbreaking. Have you even seen fine-dining restaurants in India? We spent $220 for four people and left feeling cheated.People who hype this place are honestly just falling for marketing.
And the worst part?
They deliberately served 4 pieces on plates that are supposed to have only 3, didn’t inform us upfront, let us eat, and then quietly added the extra piece to the bill. That is CHEATING.  Smiling, apologising, and still taking the money doesn’t make it okay.
Taste was fine.  Definitely not worth the glamour pricing, and dishonesty.

Also, the so-called “free dessert” they gave after that guessing game was rose kesari—and even that was done poorly. First of all, it was barely a spoonful. Second, it was not even cooked properly. Kesari is supposed to be cohesive, not grainy and broken. This felt like some half-cooked, raw semolina.

And before this place assumes I’m some random person who hasn’t experienced fine dining, (your theme is home style food, however the experience you offer falls under fine dine, priced as it is) let me be very clear: I have eaten at places like Avartana (ITC Hotels) and J Hind, which are genuinely top-tier fine-dining South Indian restaurants. This experience simply did not meet the standard it claims.

First of all, this is a modern Indian restaurant, so the dishes have a contemporary twist, either in their presentation or in some of the ingredients.

All the other dishes were also excellent and not too spicy for our taste. Not that I don’t enjoy spicy food, but I appreciated that the flavors were well balanced, allowing us to really taste all the ingredients.

When we visited, the restaurant was fairly quiet, which gave us the chance to chat with both the waiters and the owner. We even exchanged phone numbers with the owner in case he ever visits our country. P.S. Send us a WhatsApp with your number so we can save it 🙂

Overall, it was a fantastic dining experience and a great dinner. I’ll leave the detailed judgment of the food to the locals, but from my side, everything was excellent, and I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Singapore or if I return myself.

The food is absolutely amazing and the staff incredibly friendly and accommodating. The 4 stars on the atmosphere is only because the it was way too cold inside, which made the experience just a notch shy of perfect.
Booked table in advance

Restaurant Name: Poh Cheu Soon Kueh and Ang Ku Kueh
Reviews: This soon kueh and ang ku kueh shop or stall within a kopitiam in Alexandra is famous in Singapore for the aforementioned two traditional Chinese savoury and sweet kuehs. And in the case of the latter, the variety of ang ku kuehs here is very very wide, but I still prefer the traditional filling of yellow bean paste therein. As for savoury kuehs, the shop or stall also sells the traditional Teochew png kueh, ku chai kueh and glutinous rice, which are also very good. However, please be prepared to queue to order, because as mentioned, this shop or stall is famous and... very popular - seeing a constant stream of customers all day.

Restaurant Name: Poh Cheu Soon Kueh and Ang Ku Kueh
Reviews:
My sis bought frequently. I prefer the bamboo shoot kueh (ah ma soon kueh) facing road. But i would buy the abacus from poh cheu until 2yrs ago. Today(and 3wks ago) bought again to reconfirm the abacus *yam taste is still good..apparantly indeed the abacus standard drop.

LAST TIME the abacus used to be fragrant with mushroom & dried shrimps and the abacus infused with good flavour of yam but Not now. Lack of oomph (really)..more flour than yam and *Omg 2-3 strands of mushroom n short of dried shrimps fragrant. Probably they cut down on ingredient to save cost? ..Not good. Wisb they can keep up their old.gpod taste. Getting way much pricer too.

Restaurant Name: Poh Cheu Soon Kueh and Ang Ku Kueh
Reviews:
Many raved about this so I thought it would be a nice experience to taste the items since it’s a long journey there. I did not even complain about the queue, as I expected it before reaching. Was more annoyed at the elderly cashier staff than anything else.

Bought 5 soon kuehs, 5 bamboo shoot kuehs, 5 rice kuehs and 2 AKKs. Paid and stood aside to check on my purchase. The cashier staff attended to the customer after me. I told her that there were no sweet sauce and chilli condiments packed in my bag. She told me to bring the bag to show her their omission! I have not even answered her, the staff beside her immediately said she forgot to pack the condiments for me and quickly gave me the pathetic 2 packets of sweet sauce and 2 packets of chilli. I’m like I just paid less than 1 minute ago and why would someone even want to cheat you of the condiments? Your boss’ business thriving not because you help them save these few pathetic packets of condiments la! What a distasteful first experience! *roll eyes*

Reviews: Delicious Ang Ku Kueh and abacus ❤️

Restaurant Name: Poh Cheu Soon Kueh and Ang Ku Kueh
Reviews: A true taste of childhood at Poh Cheu the one stall I can never miss! I visited monthly for the handmade Soon Kueh and Ang Ku Kueh. They are simply nostalgic and full of authentic flavour. Every bite brings back sweet memories of old-school snacks done right. Especially love the variety of Soon Kueh fillings tapioca, chives, and bamboo shoots! Love the soft and fragrant kueh skin. The 算盘子 - yam abacus seeds is another must-try, chewy and comforting with great texture. For anyone who loves traditional kueh, this is a cannot-miss, must-visit stall. Truly timeless and delicious! #PohCheu #SoonKueh #AngKuKueh #TraditionalKueh #ChildhoodFlavours #SingaporeEats #HeritageFood #FoodieSingapore #算盘子 #YamAbacus

Queue wasn't too long but most things were already sold out. I was given a choice of mee rebus or tahu goreng. Tried their mee rebus and was pleasantly surprised. The gravy was rich, starch and sweet - the way I like it. Good and economical meal. Will come back in due course to try their Soto.

Ordered mee rebus for $3.50, but the portion felt more like a kids’ meal. The noodles, which are usually served in long strands, were oddly cut into shorter pieces. While the taste was acceptable, there are far better and more value-for-money mee rebus or mee soto options elsewhere; Haig Road, Bedok Interchange, and Margaret Drive, to name a few. I won’t be returning.

4 star, Michelin is a sham.  This is my super honest review. Never in 40 years of my life have I ever got such a pathetic plate of Mee Rebus. The noodles, supposed to be served in long strands, were instead cut up into shorter pieces. The noodles were so little, it did not fill up the plate. You could literally just use a spoon to eat. The only solace was a whole egg. For $3.50 this is a shameful standard. My mother used to sell mee rebus daily and I know what a quality portion looks like. I can't believe this Malay stall would stoop to this low just to cut cost. Tourists come here to try our local food and yet you serve this measly portion. You want to run a food stall, don't cheat your customers. Serve food with sincerity. Makcik you better wake up. Buat malu la. Tak ikhlas lebih baik tutup kedai je.

The platter of starters which included the popular seaweed dish, fried yams, trotters and salt and pepper, and classic lor mee were tasty and enjoyable. Desserts are light and refreshing, the fried durian puree is a local favourite.

My first visit to Quenino so I thought the Amex Love Dining menu would be a good introduction
Chef de Cuisine Sugatha Asokan is of mixed Indian and Chinese origin and her dishes lean on both her roots, with the accent on sustainability.
All the six dishes were delicious, my favourites being the house-made flatbread with flower crab and peppercorn and the scallop with razor clam and fermented chili.
The luxury ambience and impeccable service matched the fine dining experience.
Certainly worth a return visit!
Excellent service, highly knowledgeable and friendly. Opened up a new experience to Asian ingredients prepared - well-balanced and tastefully good.

Booked this place for Valentines’ dinner. Food was not bad, I loved the proteins. Service was beyond terrible.

Our first dish was served with no explanation of the entire menu, no cutleries. Confusing.

Subsequently post dinner, we’d asked for the staff to help us take a photo with their centerpiece. The photos all came back super blur and unfocused. Again, confusing. We asked the staff to retake the photos and she gladly obliged.

Finally, I paid the bill and we sat there for a good 10 mins after that. Just when we were about to leave, the staff came back with another receipt. Said she undercharged us, I tried to clarify and the response I got? “Didn’t you notice the bill amount was odd?” At this point, I knew I had definitely overpaid for the dinner even if it was the correct amount at the end.

By the way, there were only three tables that night.

To be honest, the good are good, creativity in food creation is solid! Service staffs are very friendly and can explain well on every dish. Restaurant atmosphere are great. Love their special bottled tea.
However, food ratio vs price: they are to be considered more expensive than some of the fine dining in value. The portion are just too small and a little stingy for the price they charged.

Valentine's Day 6 course menu.  Had not heard of this place (or Artyzen Singapore), but constantly saw good reviews when searching for somewhere nice on Valentine's Day.  Highly recommend for date night, the thing that really stands out is the service and the passion that both the serving staff and chief's share.  Gizher Viray was our server, outstanding thru the entire meal, made the experience enjoyable.  Julie made sure glass was full of Champagne or water without being asked.  Now to the food - we were impressed with the dishes and presentation.  Amur Caviar dish was interesting mixing so many flavors & River Prawn was tasty with Brussel Sprout & Mango.  Star of the night was the Stone Axe Wagyu with variations of garlic, melted in your mouth.  Definitely would return for another "date night", staff goes above and beyond to make the whole experience delightful.

We had the 6 course Valentine’s Dinner. Overall it didn’t meet our expectations, considering restaurant’s Michelin recommendation. Several dishes were quite blend, even the accompanying sauces couldn’t flavour up the taste adequately.
One can see the chef has pretensions but unfortunately, the food simply misses the finesse.

Had a joint bday celebration with the bff at Quenino and the experience was wonderful 🎂✨ We booked under Amex, where the menu is curated specially for Amex Love Dining reservations.

We really appreciated the thoughtful execution — a vegetarian set was prepared for my friend and a standard set for me, while keeping both menus closely aligned so we could share a similar dining experience.

The food was excellent, with refreshing flavours and well-balanced Asian influences. Hats off to Chef de Cuisine Sujatha Asokan and the team, and special thanks to Julie Jeon HyeJun for the warm, kind and attentive service that made the experience comfortable and welcoming.

A lovely celebration overall — would gladly return 😊

An absolutely impeccable dining experience from start to finish. The service was flawless—warm, attentive, and genuinely thoughtful without ever feeling intrusive. The team made us feel welcomed and well cared for throughout the entire meal.

The food was nothing short of extraordinary. Each dish was elevated, playful, and creatively executed, showcasing both technique and imagination. Every bite revealed layers of flavor and contrasting textures that kept surprising and delighting the palate. It’s the kind of cuisine that feels both refined and exciting, where familiar ingredients are transformed into something memorable.

The presentation deserves special mention—beautifully composed, intentional, and artistic without being overdone. You can clearly see the level of thought and care behind every plate.

Overall, a truly standout experience that delivers on service, creativity, and flavor. A must-visit for anyone who appreciates thoughtful, modern dining done exceptionally well.

We recently dined at Quenino, celebrating a birthday. Quenino promotes itself as a Michelin selected restaurant and we found the restaurant decor impressive - believing we had made the correct choice for a memorable birthday experience.

Best Thosai in Singapore. I've had thosai from ayer rajah to tekka to geylang and changi village and none compares to here in terms of price and taste.

IMPORTANT things to note -

Queue time after official 'opening' 7am+ is around 40mins to an hour or even longer at times as more time goes usually. This is because the regulars know to go early (around 6am+), order comfortably early and collect early. But it does make new buyers think these people came after them yet got their orders before them. Please note there are extreme regulars who have their usual paid advance orders on a weekly basis already and only show up 7am+ to sit around for collection. That is how good they are.

Also, newcomers or entitled people tend to misunderstand this particular type of busy hawker conditions. Specifically below;

The aunty is not intentionally rude. She is very busy and also keeping placed orders memorized. More manpower won't resolve the issue since the stall is small, like the size of it, literally. Just because you're next in line impatiently waiting for your order to be taken doesn't mean it'll be soon. There are alot of pending orders taken before yours that needs to be done first before she can take yours. Imagine yourself working like that day after day and dealing with numerous people daily who just have no empathy and expect restaurant and above level of smile and service. Positivity coming towards you must begin with you generating positivity towards others, make your day brighter by trying to brighten others. Expecting someone who is already overwhelmed to be the driving force for your own positive experience is just shameless of you.

So please do not be entitled and think you must be given a priority over others or be incoherent when placing your orders or be fussy that you're not being 'served' like a VIP in a fine dining establishment with a ready fake and practiced smile along with your oh-so-deluded wine selection list.

She will ask you what your order is when she can commit it to memory for you so just wait patiently and enunciate your order clearly and concisely when called upon. When you become a familiar face, you will have been there enough to see it is a shared experience, not just in one direction.

Alternatively, as mentioned, you can go early. Place your order comfortably at 6am like the regulars and come back later at 7am+ and just sit/stand around the area visibly so she can see you are there waiting to pack it fresh for you to collect. She will call you by looking directly at you and vocally asking you to come collect your order so please do not be too absorbed whilst being on your phone.

Takeaway is recommended as you can enjoy it more comfortably at home provided it is not too far away (under an hour is best). Unlike tekka thosai and most others, this doesn't rapidly drop in quality after packed. They do not use pre-made batter. That is why it is softer and stays fresher for longer. Downside; once they run out, they run out. And that is fairly quick for market standards. Usually by or around noon since they use same batter for thosai and appam etc.

Admittedly, this place is not for everyone. Some people cannot see past the delusion that the world revolves around them after all. You may feel happier in a sit down establishment with someone coming to you for your order. Rajarani will not be lacking in orders without yours so never fear.

To others who aren't as deluded, lets face it, at $4 per masala / 2 plain thosai, you're already getting a deal at that quality. Try one of those $5.50 masalas at hawkers where they HAVE to make it thin and crispy because its too grainy to make thick without being uneatable with watery and digusting red chutney and then you'll hope this stall stays in business for a long long time.

It’s was sometime back that I ate here. That was when the original owners were operating then. There was constant queue and porridge usually sold out by 9/10 am! It was good; actually excellent Hainanese porridge. Then they retired and the youngsters took over. The queue shorten and I’m uncertain if it’s still good. So today I tried. Well I must said the youngsters are doing well. Porridge is still good, liver pieces are cooked just right not overly cooked and pork slices are tender. Am very pleased to say they have done well and even achieved Michelin gourmand. I guess the youngsters have more porridge so it doesn’t sold out too early and that’s good. Oh they open every day too. So if you’re in mood for Hainanese porridge and you’re in Redhill area go try it.

Long queue as usual when I visited on 08 Feb 25 at 9.20am. Open from 6am till 1pm (or sold out). Reasonable price at $4 (+20c for takeaway container).

Michelin rated in 2024.

Porridge is smooth but not as smooth as Cantonese porridge from canton paradise or imperial treasure.

They used new rice to cook the porridge and it is fragrant

The pork slices, liver are very tender.
The pork balls with salted fish is also good.

Was surprised they won 1 Michelin Star in 2024.
Pork porridge ($5 for larger bowl + $0.50 for egg + $1.50 added pork liver) - Large, fresh pork liver slices. Good porridge texture.

Redhill Pork Porridge is my go-to whenever I’m craving porridge. I’ve tried porridge from so many places, but this is still the best for me. The texture is always perfect, and the flavors are spot on. The owners are super friendly, and the service is really quick too. It’s always consistent and never disappoints. Highly recommend if you’re in the area — but be early cos they tend to sell out by 1-2pm.
Michelin 2024 porridge. Opens 6:30am - 1pm (or sold out).

Mar 2026
We were looking forward to trying the new eatery at National Gallery.  The place is nice, with clean lines dotted with Peranakan inspired photos and decor.  It is set up ala canteen style, which is okay.  You order at the counter, pick up your food when the buzzer sounds, and return your tray at the end of the meal.

Whereas the eatery at PLQ ranked 4 - 5 stars, here we only gave 3 stars.  Staff were unsure of the dishes when we ordered.  Also, the food was not as tasty.  The chicken curry was good and reminded me of what grandma used to cook (also like NS Amoy can chicken).  Ah, nostalgia.

The missus found the pork buak keras to be sour and one dimensional, and did not enjoy the fried tauhu.  There was too much lemak in the sayur lodeh which, to me, made it sweet.  The egg was a largish piece but was also a tad bland.  Perhaps there should be sliced onions in it.  The archar was very good.  Portions were good and we were quite full at the end.

We added the sets of drink and kueh.  The kosui and bingka were nice, even if the bingka was on the softer/wet side.

Drinks were served in takeaway paper cups, which was a tad strange.  It was also disconcerting to see large groups of tourists and students ambling across the eatery to use the exit/entrance.

Dec 2024
Hosted some friends to lunch here and it was largely enjoyable.  The lunch menu has changed though, and it is now mostly nasi lemak with various options and sides.

We enjoyed the fried chee cheong fun and ayam Pelencheng so much that we ordered another portion of each.  The gerang assam fish was also nice, while the sambal prawns was a tiny portion for the price, but tasty.

Surprisingly, the chickpea with string hoppers was not a favourite, and most found the chickpea curry to be powdery and slightly sour in taste.

Service by Anthony and the team was very friendly, and efficient.  We will be back to try the dinner dishes.

2022
Had quite a lovely lunch, with attentive service by Jeremy.  Chef Damian himself made it a point to stop at each table and even delivered some dishes, which was a plus for diners.

The food was mostly hits.  We loved the fried cheong fun the best, and the dish had wok hei and was super tasty. The prawns were fresh and the towgay was crispy.  The Sri Lankan chicken curry went well with the hoppers, so much so that we ordered an extra portion of the carbs.  I liked the nasi lemak rice, which was fragrant and fluffy (it is cooked through an authentic and traditional, if tedious,  process of multiple steps) and the fried chicken was marinated well and tasty.  The chilli was sweet, rather than spicy though.

The hakka fried pork was okay - I did not really enjoy the dish, but the other diners liked it.  It went well with the chilli and the specially plum-pickled diced tomatoes, though a drop of cecap manis could perhaps also elevate the flavour.  We were recommended the Limpeh sliders, and we thought it was an imaginative take on the dish, with beef and diced cucumbers sandwiched in a prata-like case.  The beef was reminiscent in taste of corned beef hash, but the dish was a tad on the oily side.

As we were quite full by then, we opted for the four piece dessert set, comprising kueh kosui, deep fried ang ku kueh, custard, and custard with yam.  The kuehs were okay, with the kueh kosui being the best.  Coffee, sadly, was from a machine and pretty ordinary.

A big group of us had a wonderful lunch gathering at Rempapa! A big shout out to Uma and her staff for ensuring that we were all well taken care of in terms of our food orders, our seating arrangements and that everything was well in place. The food was good especially the Satay and the nasi lemak! We will definitely be back!

Toast is not bad, however, in the menu it states French toast comes with butter, but in reality the chef said it doesn’t. Either the menu isn’t updated or the chef is misinformed.

Tables were dirty, nobody cleaned the stains or food crumbs. 50% of the empty tables were uncleaned and stained.

Service was slow - we stood there for 10min with the staff ignoring us and minding their own business. Later, when we order food shown in the menu, the staff said they don’t serve it. To clarify, menu states the food is served between 3.30pm to 6pm. We ordered at 4pm, yet the staff sounded impatient and rude when she kept telling us none of our choices are being served. As a customer, this is unacceptable to me, especially in an area full of tourists. Just my ten cents.

You mean this is the standard for Singapore Master Chef Judge????

The is the most depressing butter toast I ever had. Cold when served, butter anyhow spread on. Tastes like margarine and not butter.

Staff was more eager to clean up the kitchen area so they can close shop and leave on time, so they just start serving paper cups. Thankfully my toast came in a proper plate, would have stood up and left if they were to give me paper plates, but have to deal with plastic fork…

Tea was tasteless, even Lipton tea taste better.

In disbelief that this place is being run to the ground at National Gallery.

Take your money elsewhere better.

Come from breakfast and stay for lunch.

The shokopan kaya toast was a piece of artwork, yet so delicate with the right amount of toastiness and fluffiness. The kaya was beautifully balanced not too sweet.

But the soft boiled eggs, wow! The egg yolk was super creamy and the whites were so running.

Great breakfast!
Was excited to try the kueh platter. The salat and kosui were good but the rest were bad. can consider letting customers order Ala carte instead

Manage your expectations and it’ll be fine.

I decided to visit after being inspired from watching Chef Damian documentary, decided to travel downtown to give this a try.

What I liked:
- Staff performed well under pressure. I went during lunchtime and staff was able to complete the orders on time and food looks well prepared, they were also extremely polite despite the pressure from long queue of customers waiting, from the staff taking the orders, preparing the food and even the tray cleaners. Service was really commendable
- Spacious seatings, very open air hawker-like arrangements but with quality table and chairs, giving the cozy vibes for people to relax and chit chat while eating.
- Price is affordable even with their Michelin status. $9.90 for a meal and $2.08 for kopi in aircon setting. The portion size makes it very value for money as the plating and serving does give the elevated vibes.

The only thing I wasn’t impressed with was the food. Ayam berempah marination was okay at best, sambal tasted more salt than savoury without any other elements like spiciness or that kick. The food is okay but one does come with very high expectations. I guess the price giving the settings does compensate for this. I do recommend the otah but I feel you can find similar taste from some homemade versions as well.

Overall don’t come in expecting 5 star version of local cuisine and it will be fine. Everything else was great.

We went for lunch on a Friday and were pleasantly surprised by the food. The chicken curry had a nice level of spice and the meat was cooked well. The pork dish was well seasoned, although a few pieces were a bit chewy. The space itself was clean and comfortable, making it a relaxed spot for a casual lunch.

#2nd review# (a year later)
They have relocated to the National Gallery Museum and now offer a more streamlined menu. Some of the lunch nasi lemak sets were quite a good value at $9.90. I personally enjoyed the lamb shank rendang nasi lemak set ($29.9). The kueh was good too.

#1st review#
Overall dishes were pretty good! My favourite dish was the Kueh Pie Tie, while the Hakka Fried Pork wasn't as impressive. Important note: There's a $30 corkage fee per bottle.
If you’re going to charge GST at a food kiosk, state your prices clearly.

Nice cafe in the middle of town. A cool respite during the hot weather. Food was good but more importantly was the good service. My friend accidently spilt my drink and the service team was very prompt in helping us to clean up the spill. They even gave us another drink. Unexpected small acts of kindness really brightens up my day. Thank you.

My husband and I enjoyed the delicious food in a very grand and peaceful environment. The nasi lemak sets that we have ordered were very well made. The nasi was lemongrass forward in taste which was deliciously refreshing. The flavour of the sambal was unfamiliar to me but in a very good way. As most will expect the sambal for nasi lemak to be on the sweeter flavour profile but this one has a sour profile with the addition of tamarind.

I was very impressed with braised cabbage side dish that came with the nasi lemak set. I was brimming with ingredients such as tempeh, tau gua and jackfruit. The braising sauce was loaded with spices and dried shrimps.

The food were well made with lots of care. The host even came over to check in with us as we dine. We didn't expect that because this is a causal dining concept. A very nice touch to the dining experience. Keep up the good work! I would highly recommend this place to my friends.

Not allowing reservation gives a false impression that this new place might be crowded and people might give it a miss.
Old rempapa was way better.
Fried ang ku kueh was the best kueh but it's not sold anymore at the new venue.
Nasi lemak taste is weak, very disappointed.
The way the nasi lemak is sold along with sides should be reconsidered.
Sambal sotong was the nicest, exceptional.
Tray has zero friction.

Ordered the prawns and pork belly entrees. Shrimp was overcooked, tough and chewy. Pork belly was not tender. Everything lacking flavor.
The side dishes were bland.

The restaurant itself is nice and clean. But the food is not worth the high price. Total was $45 SGD.

Heard good things about Rempapa and I was delighted to find it opened at a nearer location. The cafe offers affordable lunch menus, and food was generally ok. We ordered the Kueh platter which was super yummy and it’s worth adding this option for the lunch special, which gave one a drink and 2 pieces of kuehs.

We went as a large group on one of their earlier opening days and the service was attentive - the staff apologised for a slightly slower service due to teething issues even though there was no need to do so (we didn’t wait that long!)
We love your staff Anthony and Uma , the best service of my visit to Spore Museum.

Underwhelming. I ordered chicken berempah nasi lemak set. The chicken was underseasoned and dry, yet somehow managed to be red and undercooked in the middle. The rest of the side dishes are just really so mediocre I had newfound appreciation for my neighbourhood nasi lemak hawkers. Sambal is too sour and lacks flavour.

It was quiet when i visited and the staff are chatting. Yet tables were not wiped after the guest leaves, so you'd see rice grains and water stains.

🟠 Rempapa by Damian D'Silva
1, St Andrew's Road, #01-02A
NATIONAL Gallery
Singapore 178957

🟠 Location = Rempapa, a casual bistro cafe by Chef Damian D 'Silva, is located within the National Gallery building.

🟠 The National Gallery building itself is just a short walk from City Hall MRT station.

🟠 Inside the building, the Rempapa Cafe is situated just next to the former Supreme Court Wing (--- where the former holding cells are).

🔵 The menu/ what they sell
*****************************
🔵 8 am till 11am ( Breakfast)  ➖️ Kaya Toast, French Toast, Egg Mayo Toast and Rempapa Shashuka.

🔵 11am till 3pm ( Lunch) ➖️ Nasi Lemak Lunch Sets starting from SGD9.90. ➡️ You can add on various side dishes like Otak-Otak, Ayam Berempah, Sambal Sotong, Sambal Prawns, Sayur Lodeh, Lamb Shank Rendang and etc.

🔵 3 pm to 6 pm ( Tea time) ➖️ Tea, coffee, Peranakan-style kueh-kueh and local heritage desserts.

🟢 Nasi Lemak Ayam Berempah set ( dapao)
***********************************
🟢 I came at around 11.20 am & ordered the Nasi Lemak Ayam Berempah set priced at SGD15.90 for takeaway.

🟢 The Nasi Lemak Ayam Berempah (SGD15.90) was a delicious and satisfying heritage-style set. ▪︎The spiced fried chicken was aromatic and crisp, pairing well with the fragrant coconut ( santan infused) rice.

✳️ Santan = means coconut milk in Malay.

🟢 The sambal added a sweet–spicy kick, complemented by the classic sides of peanuts, anchovies ( ie Ikan Bilis), and a jammy soft-boiled egg.➖️  The accompanying bowl of Sayur Lodeh was savoury and comforting, rounding off the meal beautifully.

🟢 The Teh-O ( local tea with sugar) was smooth & strong, with a pleasant tea aroma, and a gentle tannin finish -- nicely balanced without being too sweet.

🟪 Service = 🟪 I ordered at the cashier's counter and paid by Visa credit card. ➖️ A timer buzzer is given to you, and when your food is ready, the timer will buzz, and you go to the counter to collect.➖️ Just like in a canteen.

🟪 Service was quick & efficient, and the staff generally pleasant and helpful.

🟡 Seats = Indoor aircon-seats and outdoor alfresco seats in the courtyard are available. 🟡 There are ceiling fans at the outdoor area.

🟡 All in all, the food was delicious and the prices were reasonable for my pocket. ➖️ 🔴 My photos were taken both during daytime and night time as I had visited Rempapa Cafe twice.

✴️ dated 29 Nov 2025 Sat.

I had the sambal sotong lunch set.

I was rather disappointed that the sambal sotong was just steamed sotong with sambal on it. I was expecting stir fried sambal sotong. I was too excited seeing sotong on the menu, I just ordered without reading the fine print on the menu. Sambal is salty and too spicy.

Sayur lodeh had a lot of ingredients, even had jackfruit which was a plus. But can be more lemak and less watery.

Rice and condiments were just average for me, nothing memorable.

Will not visit again.

The service was great, friendly and helpful staff. However the basic nasi lemak plus chicken wing was a tad salty and dry. Egg was hard boiled instead of the classic fried egg. Maybe other food options are much better which I did not try.
Tea was instant 3 in 1 in disposable cup which was unexpected. Will be great to have real brewed tea/ coffee that aligns with the local charm and theme of their food.
Tray was also too small for their large plates.
I am hoping you guys will improve as the location is really a great place to chill. Bring back the old standard of your food from your previous location at PLQ.

​Had the immense pleasure of dining at Rempapa, a Peranakan gem, and I'm not just raving about the food—which was spectacular—but the heartwarming service  by Jennifer that made the entire experience unforgettable.

Jennifer was attentive and offered insightful recommendations for the dishes. We settled on the Asam Babi,Ayam Buah Keluak, Papaya Masak Rempah Titek and Sayur Kacang Rempah Titek.

​She would check in on us and, when she noticed my brother finishing his first bowl of rice shes approached my brother to enquire he requires an additional seving of rice. It was thoughtful, intuitive, and deeply caring service.

​If you’re looking for authentic Peranakan food served with a side of the most sincere, heartwarming service you’ll ever encounter, you must visit Rempapa.
Pricy and the food taste was moderate.

I visited Rempapa on the night of 17th September and was absolutely blown away by the experience. The food was delicious, the kueh soft and flavourful, but what truly stood out was the service. The team, especially Anthony and his colleague (Sorry I didn't get his name) was one of the best dining crews I have ever encountered. They were attentive, checking in often to ensure we were comfortable and enjoying our meal.

What really touched us was their thoughtfulness near closing time. Instead of rushing us out like many restaurants might, they noticed that my friend (whose birthday we were celebrating) and I were still deep in conversation. They kindly offered us a table outside, even helping to move our leftover kueh and drinks out so we could continue chatting while they prepared to close. Later, before leaving for the night, they even checked if we needed water or anything else.

This level of warmth and sincerity made us feel truly valued as customers. It was one of the most welcoming dining experiences I’ve ever had. Thank you to the Rempapa team for making my friend’s birthday so special and for going above and beyond in your service. Truly, great job.

Comparing to other perankan’s this is not worth the money. Nothing special. I will not go there. There are better ones that offer better ayam Buah Keluak go for in other location.

1. Dish Ayam Buah Keluak - wait a while, food serve warm not hot. Taste so so not that fantastic

2. Dish Otak - the saving grace but kind of miserable for 3 and you got charge sgd 18 for 3 pieces

3. Jasmine rice - serve warm not hot for sgd 3

4. Peranakan chap chye - should be hot and this should be fried when order not sure what the chef is doing. This is no excuse such restaurant should serve food like that

Bland tasting food. Hardly any taste of peranakan. Lucky it is closing soon.

Two stars was meant for the warm hospitality. Love the lady who served us. But the chef needs to change. Only the Chap Chye still has some lingering flavors but the duck soup and pork dish were not even food court standard. Not sweet not salty and no taste of any spices.
Food was superlicious! Service was fantastic too. We were served by Jennifer very warmth, friendly & diligent at work too. We will definitely come bck to see Jennifer at National Gallery again!

Impressed by the long list of awards achieved by Restaurant Born in Singapore, I decided to give it a go. Based on my experiences, I would conclude that they deserve all exceptional reviews.

It serves French-Chinese fusion. It interestingly combines French gastronomy techniques with Chinese and Malaysian flavours. What I like most is its creative storytelling. This definitely elevates my overall dining experience.

Go for the kitchen counter seats to watch the chefs at work. It is part of the culinary journey you cannot miss in Singapore!

It might have been an unusually 'off' day for them. Service was disappointing to say the least. Apart from not understanding most of what was said about the dishes the entire night we got our tongues burnt because we were not warned that the snack was extremely hot! Although they tried service recovery   I wasn't expecting such thoughtless service from a michilen restaurant. That already set the night out to be a bomb out.
The food got better and bolder as the menu unfolded. But to be honest the starting dishes were unexciting.
Although it is nice to have a theme and not to be limited by seasonal ingredients,how this conbeyed to the customer is important.

Food is delicious and innovative, without being too adventurous for my liking. Ambience is fantastic: Airy and inviting. But what was just as amazing were the team: Chef Zor was attentive to all, the team were warm, inviting and efficient. Will be back very soon for more!!!

We LOVE dining here and have made it an annual event every time we are in Singapore around CNY, same seats, different experience. This round we were with the first diners to try the new season menu. I will let the pictures do the talking, but we are always impressed with the food, flavours, the thought behind each dish. The tea pairing is always one of highlights. The Chef & Team do an incredible job. I think the price is well worth it (and restaurant styling is beautiful). I've spent a lot more in other high end restaurants and have been disappointed time and time again. Born is what I use as my comparison / baseline.

Restaurant Born offers an elegant fine dining experience with a focus on contemporary, seasonal cuisine. The tasting menus are thoughtfully curated, beautifully plated, and full of balanced flavors. Service is attentive and knowledgeable, enhancing the intimate ambience. It’s premium-priced, but ideal for special occasions or for those seeking a refined culinary journey.

We had the set lunch (Friday only).  I wasn’t impressed.  Except for the first 2 courses which were unique, the other courses were just mediocre, so many were accompanied by deep fried items and you don’t pay $238pp to have deep fried food do you?

In terms of atmosphere, although it is housed in a historical building, I find the restaurant decor and table arrangements uninviting.  The counter seats are also directly under the sun (glass roof) and it was so warm and glaring.

Restaurant Born is an intimate fine dining restaurant offering a refined menu of contemporary cuisine with innovative flavors and elegant presentation. The dishes are thoughtfully crafted using high-quality, seasonal ingredients. The ambiance is sophisticated and cozy, making it ideal for special occasions or romantic dinners. Service is attentive, knowledgeable, and polished, ensuring a seamless and memorable culinary experience. Restaurant Born provides a modern and elevated dining journey for guests seeking a premium gastronomic experience in Singapore.

I loved the elegant atmosphere!
Experience was very beautiful and food was very delicious.

此趟新加坡最愛的一家！也是肯定會想二訪的餐廳，一星實至名歸，甚至都覺得主廚創意跟廚藝不斷精進的話，有很高的機率會拿下二星😍 除了料理每一道都有滿滿的記憶點又美味，店內的裝潢也是相當講究！藝術感滿分💯
